V4-01.01.text: The engine MUST retain exact accepted evidence and its provenance; no generated output may impersonate original testimony, observation, or authenticated execution.

V4-01.02.text: The engine MUST support personal continuity, project knowledge, changing state, investigations, recurring workflows, and authorized multi-agent reuse.

V4-01.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-01.03.text: The primary competitive objective is higher downstream utility at an explicitly bounded total cost, latency, and privacy exposure.

V4-01.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-01.04.text: The product MUST offer capture, recall, context, inspect, correct, forget, and health through consistent host-neutral contracts.

V4-01.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-01.05.text: Canonical evidence is immutable except authorized erasure; interpretations and derived views are revisioned, replaceable, attributable, and invalidatable.

V4-01.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-01.06.text: Local operation MUST remain useful without a cloud account, GPU, daemon, generative model, or network-accessible database.

V4-01.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-01.07.text: Neural retrieval, grounded synthesis, experience reuse, and service breadth remain contracted M1–M4 deliverables, not prerequisites for M0; installation and activation remain explicit owner choices.

V4-01.08.text: Leadership claims MUST identify tested competitors, editions, versions, workloads, reader models, budgets, and uncertainty under §54–§59.

V4-01.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-01.09.text: More stored facts, more context, or more memory use MUST NOT substitute for measured utility; negative transfer is a first-class failure.

V4-01.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-01.10.text: The engine MUST NOT execute recalled procedures, change host permissions, or silently rewrite host system prompts.

V4-02.01.section_title: Normative language, applicability, and evidence status
V4-02.01.text: Every requirement MUST map to a capability, delivery tier, owner role, implementation surface, evidence type, and acceptance scenario.

V4-02.02.section_title: Normative language, applicability, and evidence status
V4-02.02.text: Status values MUST be `unimplemented`, `partial`, `implemented_unverified`, `verified`, `deferred`, or `not_applicable`; none are inferred from test counts.

V4-02.03.section_title: Normative language, applicability, and evidence status
V4-02.03.text: `verified` MUST name executable checks and observed artifacts that cover the whole requirement, including failure and recovery behavior.

V4-02.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-02.04.section_title: Normative language, applicability, and evidence status
V4-02.04.text: A requirement shared by multiple surfaces MUST remain partial until every shipped surface passes the same invariant tests.

V4-02.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-02.05.section_title: Normative language, applicability, and evidence status
V4-02.05.text: Security, privacy, byte integrity, and deletion invariants bind every enabled feature, including experiments and compatibility adapters.

V4-02.06.section_title: Normative language, applicability, and evidence status
V4-02.06.text: A deferred requirement MUST retain its owner, reason, prerequisite, milestone, and effect on product claims; silent scope removal is prohibited.

V4-02.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-02.07.section_title: Normative language, applicability, and evidence status
V4-02.07.text: Historical documentation, vendor claims, hypotheses, local measurements, and independent reproductions MUST use distinct evidence labels.

V4-02.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-02.08.section_title: Normative language, applicability, and evidence status
V4-02.08.text: Requirement changes after approval MUST preserve old identifiers and record supersession, rationale, affected gates, and renewed evidence obligations.

V4-03.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-03.01.text: The benchmark registry MUST maintain separate manifests for every tested edition and identify inaccessible or unsupported editions explicitly.

V4-03.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-03.02.text: Comparator discovery MUST include new credible market entrants before each leadership claim and at least every 90 days during active claims.

V4-03.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-03.03.text: Holographic MUST be tested at a pinned Hermes revision; this design inspected `9ba5850e955e1068355350ed6241fb78acea120f` [R03].

V4-03.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-03.04.text: Documented capabilities MUST be implemented as product outcomes, not copied blindly as identical algorithms or infrastructure.

V4-03.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-03.05.text: Provider-specific marketing numbers MUST NOT become VERBATIM acceptance results or substitute for executed comparisons.

V4-03.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-03.06.text: Conflicting documentation MUST be recorded and resolved against the pinned edition before using the disputed behavior in a benchmark.

V4-04.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.01.text: Every nontrivial new retrieval or learning mechanism MUST receive an ablation against the simplest safe alternative.

V4-04.02.text: Exact entity intersection MUST be the reference for Holographic-style composition; HRR needs incremental benefit beyond that reference.

V4-04.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.03.text: Generated views MUST compete against extractive packs and typed templates under identical downstream reader and context budgets.

V4-04.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.04.text: Graph, hierarchy, and reflection MUST demonstrate value on long-history, multi-hop, or experience workloads rather than only short lookup fixtures.

V4-04.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.05.text: Utility feedback MUST affect relevance or recommendation, never authentic authorship, permission, or verified checker status.

V4-04.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.06.text: A winning component MAY become a profile default only after its quality, safety, cost, and recovery gates pass together.

V4-04.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.07.text: The simple baseline MUST remain runnable as a regression oracle even when a richer profile becomes recommended.

V4-04.08.text: A failed hypothesis MUST cause redesign, narrower claims, or removal from recommended routing rather than benchmark redefinition.

V4-04.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.09.text: I1–I6 MUST reuse existing pack, dependency, replay, and scheduler contracts; no independent store, facade, trust score, or permission evaluator may be introduced.

V4-04.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.10.text: I1 manifests MUST distinguish verified bytes from probabilistic semantic support and disclose inaccessible counterevidence only through safe insufficiency labels.

V4-04.11.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.11.text: I2 MUST invalidate immediately before asynchronous recomputation; reduced work cannot retain stale content or omit hidden dependencies.

V4-04.12.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.12.text: I3 MUST retain complete conditions, contradictions, safety constraints, and exact-identifier requirements; token savings from dropping them fail the experiment.

V4-04.13.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.13.text: I4 MUST evaluate held-out repositories/environments with verified outcomes; self-reports, exposures, and hypothetical trials cannot count as transfer success.

V4-04.14.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.14.text: I5 MUST propagate live erasure/revocation into branches, prohibit external side effects, and apply approved changes only through the normal fenced coordinator.

V4-04.15.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.15.text: I6 MUST keep updates tenant-local, preserve explicit owner priorities, and include deferred-readiness and stale-answer costs in its utility comparison.

V4-04.16.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-04.16.text: M5 MUST publish the six experiment dispositions, raw paired outcomes, resource costs, and prior-art comparison; innovation is accepted by measured advantage, not naming.

V4-05.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-05.01.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.01.text: F4-01 through F4-15 and F4-17 through F4-21 MUST have public-surface regressions for every reachable path; disabled later capabilities must deny explicitly and retain their unresolved functional obligations.

V4-05.02.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.02.text: The 513-child purge, cancelled-admit, corrupted-payload, purpose-crossing, and oversized-fallback fixtures MUST remain permanent regression cases.

V4-05.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-05.03.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.03.text: Claims, observations, procedures, source views, cached packs, exports, and file projections MUST share each applicable boundary test.

V4-05.04.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.04.text: Existing passing tests that encode an unsafe contract MUST be corrected with explicit compatibility notes, not treated as normative behavior.

V4-05.05.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.05.text: The standalone purge handler MUST be tested separately from ordinary purge until both use the same implementation.

V4-05.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-05.06.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.06.text: F4-16 closes only through executed evidence; implementing another harness or adding synthetic examples is insufficient.

V4-05.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-05.07.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.07.text: No new capability may be declared production-ready while a relevant F4 blocker remains unresolved.

V4-05.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-05.08.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.08.text: Probe descriptions MUST be converted into durable repository tests; temporary review scripts are not release evidence artifacts.

V4-05.09.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.09.text: W0 MUST begin at package discovery and `verbatim:register`, then exercise initialize, capture, drain, prefetch/tool recall, correction, restart, and deletion on the registered provider.

V4-05.10.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.10.text: Store-path tests MUST cover legacy-only, v3-only, both-present, neither-present, and explicit-path cases; conflicting stores require an operator decision, never a silent merge or empty replacement.

V4-05.11.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.11.text: Malformed UTF-8 tests MUST cover text imports, inline envelopes, structural events, and byte locators; replace-decoding cannot mint offsets presented as original byte ranges.

V4-05.12.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.12.text: Injected quarantine lookup failures MUST withhold affected content on every public read surface, including working-set access and compatibility APIs.

V4-05.13.section_title: Mandatory closure of the current review findings
V4-05.13.text: Session-end drain failure MUST leave the host usable while status/receipts expose the error and pending work; `except: pass` is not an acceptable success path.

V4-06.01.text: The default profile MUST be `local_rules`: SQLite authority, no network, no implicit workers, and no ambient capture.

V4-06.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-06.02.text: `local_semantic` MUST add a reviewed pinned neural encoder without requiring a service or generative model.

V4-06.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-06.03.text: `local_synthesis` MUST add explicit local-generation provisioning while preserving the same evidence, policy, and deletion contracts.

V4-06.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-06.04.text: `consented_remote` MUST enable only enumerated processors through §12; mode selection alone never grants disclosure consent.

V4-06.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-06.05.text: `team_service` MUST use an authenticated service authority; `scaled_service` additionally requires PostgreSQL conformance and S4 evidence.

V4-06.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-06.06.text: `portable` MUST expose governed projections and bundles without pretending offline recipients have current revocation knowledge.

V4-06.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-06.07.text: Capture, synthesis, sharing, connector polling, network listeners, telemetry, and automatic promotion MUST default off.

V4-06.08.text: An expansion or research feature that ships early MUST pass its full applicable requirements; its tier cannot excuse unsafe behavior.

V4-06.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-06.09.text: No profile may lower authorization, integrity, quarantine, or suppression checks to meet a performance target.

V4-06.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-06.10.text: Unfinished expansion commitments MUST remain named in the release manifest with owners and blockers, never silently removed.

V4-07.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-07.01.text: Production consumers MUST receive typed kernel/repository interfaces rather than unrestricted store connections.

V4-07.02.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/api_v3/facade.py, verbatim/export.py, verbatim/ingest.py...; no mapped executable check
V4-07.02.text: Only authority/storage modules and audited migrations MAY read plaintext evidence columns directly; a dependency rule enforces this restriction.

V4-07.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-07.03.text: Policy and model components MUST compute plans without committing; the coordinator alone applies authoritative domain effects.

V4-07.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-07.04.text: Optional retrieval/model imports MAY fail unavailable; missing governance, integrity, or suppression modules MUST fail closed.

V4-07.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-07.05.text: Engine construction MUST explicitly inject clock, caller binder, artifact registry, key provider, scheduler, and transport broker.

V4-07.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-07.06.text: No import may open stores, download artifacts, start workers, bind sockets, select providers, or inspect host credentials.

V4-07.07.text: Compatibility surfaces MUST translate into the same services; parallel implementations of recall, purge, or evidence verification are prohibited.

V4-07.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-07.08.text: Host neutrality MUST be tested with fake hosts and real adapters; package naming alone is not proof of layering.

V4-07.09.text: `register()` and the package entry point MUST construct the consolidated engine route; qualification cannot substitute direct construction of an unregistered adapter.

V4-07.10.text: Hermes, CLI, SDK, MCP, and compatibility wrappers MUST use one profile store resolver; no adapter may silently create its own version-named database.

V4-07.11.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-07.11.text: Each consolidation change MUST identify the legacy decisions/queries removed or redirected and prove old entry points cannot bypass the replacement.

V4-07.12.text: Compatibility wrappers MUST own no independent authorization, raw evidence reads, lifecycle commits, fallback packer, or default store selection.

V4-07.13.text: CI MUST trace registered calls and compare store identity, policy outcome, and receipts across surfaces; a third parallel engine or policy implementation fails architecture qualification.

V4-08.01.text: Access resolution MUST include every contributing parent's scope, purpose, lifecycle, quarantine, suppression, and retention constraints.

V4-08.02.text: Exact original text MUST require `quote`; `read` permits authorized metadata and approved derived views, not a raw-text loophole.

V4-08.03.text: Verified reads MUST authenticate payload and slice bindings to store, object, revision, locator, and digest algorithm.

V4-08.04.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/core/types_v4.py, verbatim/kernel/service.py; no mapped executable check
V4-08.04.text: In-process eligibility MUST remain bound to caller, operation, snapshot/epochs, and lifetime inside the shared engine; serialized signed leases are required only when crossing an untrusted service boundary, not for ordinary local function calls.

V4-08.05.text: A denied or unavailable dependency MUST invalidate the dependent group; returning a misleading subset is prohibited.

V4-08.06.text: Scope-local counts, titles, snippets, identifiers, and error details MUST receive the same disclosure review as primary content.

V4-08.07.text: Raw-source browsing MUST enter the ordinary kernel and packer as an explicit archive/evidence lane, never after a failed recall.

V4-08.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-08.08.text: Kernel tests MUST cover API, MCP, SDK, export, compiler, indexer, cache, replay, projection, and service paths.

V4-08.09.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/kernel/service.py, verbatim/synthesis/synthesizer.py; no mapped executable check
V4-08.09.text: A kernel failure MUST not trigger duplicate SQL, weakened checks, or an alternate unverified serialization path.

V4-08.10.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/kernel/service.py; no mapped executable check
V4-08.10.text: Python plugins running with unrestricted process access are trusted code; hostile-plugin isolation requires a separate sandboxed process.

V4-09.01.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/core/policy.py, verbatim/core/types_v4.py, verbatim/jobs/source_jobs.py; no mapped executable check
V4-09.01.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.01.text: `EffectPlan` MUST carry operation identity, input digests, expected revisions, scope epochs, producer identity, intended effects, and required follow-up jobs.

V4-09.02.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.02.text: `apply_plan` MUST verify the lease, authorization, dependencies, and expected versions inside the same transaction that writes domain effects.

V4-09.03.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.03.text: Domain revisions, provenance edges, invalidation events, operation receipts, outbox obligations, and job completion MUST commit atomically.

V4-09.04.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.04.text: A stale or cancelled worker MUST commit no new claim, derivative, index publication, outcome, or disclosure permission.

V4-09.05.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.05.text: Replaying an operation with identical input MUST return its prior receipt; reusing its key with different input MUST fail `OPERATION_CONFLICT`.

V4-09.06.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.06.text: Disclosure MUST linearize when `seal_delivery` commits after rechecking all contributing scopes and dependency versions.

V4-09.07.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.07.text: Revocation acknowledgment MUST prevent later delivery permits; earlier permitted in-flight disclosures MUST be enumerated and honestly irreversible.

V4-09.08.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.08.text: A permit not handed to its bound transport within its maximum age MUST expire and require reauthorization; default maximum age is one second.

V4-09.09.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/core/policy.py, verbatim/ingest.py, verbatim/jobs/coordinator.py...; no mapped executable check
V4-09.09.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.09.text: No database transaction may remain open while waiting for a model, connector, socket, artifact download, or user decision.

V4-09.10.note: test module docstring claims coverage in tests/jobs/test_coordinator.py; no named check (V4-61.02)
V4-09.10.section_title: Atomic effect plans and disclosure linearization
V4-09.10.text: Strict disclosure auditing MUST fail closed if its minimal receipt cannot persist; optional analytics may be buffered separately.

V4-10.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-10.01.text: Caller identity MUST bind through a trusted host, local operator launch, or verified service authentication, never a model-supplied principal field.

V4-10.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-10.02.text: Scope identity MUST distinguish tenant, owner, workspace, conversation, and audience; raw partition IDs remain opaque and stable.

V4-10.03.text: Source deduplication MUST include owning scope and origin; identical external identifiers in different scopes MUST never graft evidence together.

V4-10.04.text: Reads MUST intersect explicit scope narrowing with effective authority; omission of a scope filter MUST not mean global access.

V4-10.05.text: Cross-scope retrieval MUST require an explicit search-domain policy plus per-scope authorization for the requested purpose and output kind.

V4-10.06.text: All lookup surfaces MUST make absent and unauthorized objects indistinguishable without leaking counts, timing classes, or private labels intentionally.

V4-10.07.text: Derived audiences MUST be the intersection of contributing parent permissions, unless an independently authorized declassification operation records a new policy.

V4-10.08.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/kernel/service.py; no mapped executable check
V4-10.08.text: Principal retirement MUST invalidate grants, sessions, permits, caches, and queued work without rewriting evidence authorship.

V4-11.01.text: Purpose constraints MUST use explicit tagged forms `ANY`, `SET(values)`, and `NONE`; empty SET normalizes to NONE, never ANY.

V4-11.02.text: Delegation MUST prove effective child authority is a subset of effective parent authority across verbs, resources, purposes, expiry, and delegation depth.

V4-11.03.text: Caveats are conjunctive restrictions; delegation MUST retain or strengthen them, never remove restrictions by applying ordinary subset logic.

V4-11.04.text: Every retrieved scope MUST pass the same purpose-aware authorization function; a purpose-blind verb union is diagnostic only.

V4-11.05.text: `derive` MUST not imply `read`, `quote`, `share`, `hydrate`, or `act`; producer plaintext access requires separately authorized input access.

V4-11.06.text: Revocation MUST invalidate the entire descendant delegation chain and advance the affected authorization epochs atomically.

V4-11.07.text: A request spanning scopes MUST pin an epoch vector, not just the epoch of its initially requested scope.

V4-11.08.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/kernel/service.py; no mapped executable check
V4-11.08.text: Purpose names MUST resolve through an operator-controlled registry; retired purposes cannot authorize new operations.

V4-11.09.text: Grant evaluators MUST reject cyclic chains, excessive depth, ambiguous constraints, malformed expiry, and non-finite values.

V4-11.10.text: Property tests MUST search for authority expansion under arbitrary grant/delegation combinations, including empty sets and multiple parents.

V4-12.01.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.01.text: Document embeddings, query embeddings, reranking, judgments, synthesis, connector uploads, and diagnostics MUST use the same egress broker.

V4-12.02.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.02.text: Permits MUST bind recipient origin, account/region where applicable, purpose, payload digest, contributing scopes, consent versions, and maximum spend.

V4-12.03.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.03.text: Dispatch MUST recheck active consent, source suppression, policy epochs, and reservation availability immediately before transferring ownership to transport.

V4-12.04.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.04.text: Zero remote budget MUST prohibit dispatch, including nominally free requests whose provider pricing or quota is unknown.

V4-12.05.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.05.text: Budget reservation MUST occur atomically before network I/O; timeouts retain conservative reservations until reconciliation.

V4-12.06.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.06.text: A multi-scope payload MUST have consent for every contributing scope and recipient; the host's default scope cannot stand in for them.

V4-12.07.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.07.text: Transport endpoints MUST be allowlisted, TLS-verified, redirect-controlled, bounded, and protected against DNS rebinding and credential forwarding.

V4-12.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-12.08.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.08.text: Minimization MUST select authorized fields before heuristic redaction; secret detectors are supplementary, not disclosure authorization.

V4-12.09.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.09.text: Offline profiles MUST pass process-level network-denial tests; replacing an HTTP client with a mock is not sufficient proof.

V4-12.10.section_title: Consent, transport egress, and resource spending
V4-12.10.text: Receipts MUST persist permit-to-request correlation across crashes without retaining raw prompts or credentials by default.

V4-13.01.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.01.text: Source envelopes MUST record authenticated capture actor, claimed authorship, host, origin, external identity, media type, timestamps, scope, and consent proof.

V4-13.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-13.02.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.02.text: Source revisions MUST be immutable and content-addressable within the store's keyed identity domain; updates create revisions rather than rewriting bytes.

V4-13.03.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/core/types_v4.py; no mapped executable check
V4-13.03.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.03.text: Text locators MUST use validated UTF-8 byte ranges; empty, overlapping, malformed, or out-of-bounds ranges require explicit interpretation.

V4-13.04.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/kernel/service.py, verbatim/storage/schema_v4.py; no mapped executable check
V4-13.04.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.04.text: Integrity records MUST use domain-separated authenticated digests covering object type, identity, revision, locator, algorithm, and relevant provenance binding.

V4-13.05.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.05.text: Verified reads MUST compare digests before use; null legacy digests MUST return `legacy_unverified`, never verified provenance.

V4-13.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-13.06.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.06.text: Parsed/OCR/transcribed views MUST identify the transformer and exact parent artifact; quotations name the accepted view, not nonexistent original text bytes.

V4-13.07.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.07.text: Generated submissions MAY be canonical evidence of the submission, but MUST retain agent/model-generated provenance and cannot become human testimony.

V4-13.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-13.08.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.08.text: Metadata used for trust, checker identity, privacy, or derivation MUST be authenticated or recomputable; payload-only digests are insufficient.

V4-13.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-13.09.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.09.text: Deduplication MUST preserve independent attribution and retention policies rather than collapsing identical statements into one ownerless fact.

V4-13.10.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/retrieval/package.py; no mapped executable check
V4-13.10.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.10.text: Integrity diagnostics MUST distinguish corrupt, missing, erased, unverified, and verified evidence without exposing inaccessible object details.

V4-13.11.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.11.text: Textual capture MUST either strictly validate UTF-8 before acceptance or create a declared transformed view with an exact source mapping; screening and harvesting must consume that same accepted representation.

V4-13.12.section_title: Canonical evidence, accepted views, and integrity
V4-13.12.text: Decode, screening, or quarantine-lookup failure MUST never imply clean content; malformed text cannot be admitted through replace-decoding, fallback recall, or host-hook error suppression.

V4-14.01.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.01.text: Accepted capture MUST atomically persist evidence, consent binding, screening disposition, operation receipt, and required processing obligations.

V4-14.02.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.02.text: Each receipt MUST expose independent `accepted`, `screened`, `lexical_ready`, `semantic_ready`, `derived_ready`, and `failed` states.

V4-14.03.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.03.text: `wait_ready(receipt, capabilities, deadline)` MUST wait for that receipt's dependency DAG or return pending/error without inventing readiness.

V4-14.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-14.04.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.04.text: SDKs and adapters MUST enqueue only unless explicitly configured to own a documented worker lifecycle; imports never start workers.

V4-14.05.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.05.text: `drain` MUST report processed, succeeded, failed, deferred, and still-pending counts; reaching a caller limit is not queue completion.

V4-14.06.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.06.text: A drain MUST reconsider newly enqueued higher-priority work before continuing lower-priority work, while honoring the caller's absolute deadline.

V4-14.07.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.07.text: Session-end drain failures MUST be visible and durable; host shutdown MUST not discard accepted obligations or pretend derived readiness.

V4-14.08.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.08.text: Duplicate capture keys with identical input MUST converge; different input under the same key MUST fail or create an explicit revision.

V4-14.09.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.09.text: Fresh-store MCP capture MUST require explicit retention consent and remain agent-attributed unless a trusted host handle supplies authorship.

V4-14.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-14.10.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.10.text: Pending evidence MAY be browsed only through an explicit authorized archive mode with pending labels and ordinary screening/budget enforcement.

V4-14.11.section_title: Capture, durable readiness, and explicit draining
V4-14.11.text: Registered host hooks MUST surface drain/capture failures through status or a safe callback, preserve accepted obligations, and never report session-end processing complete solely because the hook returned normally.

V4-15.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-15.01.text: Text segmentation MUST preserve offsets, speaker changes, quoted blocks, negation, conditions, headings, tables, code fences, and adjacent required context.

V4-15.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-15.02.text: Code and tool records MUST preserve commands, arguments, paths, test identifiers, errors, patches, and observed exit status without paraphrasing.

V4-15.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-15.03.text: Parsers MUST run with byte, recursion, decompression, CPU, memory, and output bounds in a constrained process where applicable.

V4-15.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-15.04.text: HTML/PDF extraction MUST preserve document version and location mapping; hidden text and parser disagreement MUST remain inspectable.

V4-15.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-15.05.text: OCR and transcription MUST record confidence, language, model revision, source interval/region, and unverifiable portions without filling gaps.

V4-15.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-15.06.text: Multimodal similarity MUST not authorize disclosure of the underlying artifact; returned previews require independent evidence access checks.

V4-15.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-15.07.text: Chunk identities MUST be stable under repeated processing with the same source and segmenter revision; changed segmenters create new projection generations.

V4-15.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-15.08.text: Overflow MUST identify omitted ranges and incomplete context groups; successful ingestion must not conceal truncation.

V4-16.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-16.01.text: The extractor registry MUST support deterministic patterns, typed host events, local discriminative models, and opt-in generative proposal producers.

V4-16.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-16.02.text: Every proposed claim MUST contain evidence locators, subject candidates, predicate, value, polarity, modality, conditions, temporal interpretation, and producer manifest.

V4-16.03.text: Proposed quotations MUST be resolved from supplied locators by the kernel; model-emitted quotation strings are never trusted as byte matches.

V4-16.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-16.04.text: Missing fields MUST remain unknown rather than fabricated; unresolved reference or attribution prevents automatic active admission.

V4-16.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-16.05.text: Generative extraction MUST use bounded schemas and record unsupported propositions, rejected locators, ambiguity, and abstention rates.

V4-16.06.text: User topic policies MUST steer retention without suppressing deletion, consent withdrawal, corrections, or security events.

V4-16.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-16.07.text: Automatic admission MUST use a calibrated risk policy; high-impact, sensitive, conflicting, or weakly grounded claims require review.

V4-16.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-16.08.text: Rules-only capture MUST retain useful evidence even when interpretation abstains; it must not masquerade as full natural-language understanding.

V4-16.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-16.09.text: The same interpretation pipeline MUST process explicit remember requests, imports, connector text, and host captures without privileged shortcuts.

V4-16.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-16.10.text: Extraction quality MUST be measured separately from retrieval and reader accuracy, including omissions, wrong attribution, and false updates.

V4-17.01.section_title: Entities, reference resolution, and multilingual coverage
V4-17.01.text: Entity identifiers MUST be scope-bound, with separate names, aliases, roles, source references, and merge/split history.

V4-17.02.section_title: Entities, reference resolution, and multilingual coverage
V4-17.02.text: Alias candidates MUST combine exact identifiers, contextual evidence, and optional semantic similarity; similarity alone cannot authorize identity merging.

V4-17.03.section_title: Entities, reference resolution, and multilingual coverage
V4-17.03.text: Pronouns and deictic references MUST resolve only within declared context windows and record competing candidates or ambiguity.

V4-17.04.section_title: Entities, reference resolution, and multilingual coverage
V4-17.04.text: User, assistant, quoted third party, hypothetical subject, and reported speaker MUST remain distinct throughout extraction and retrieval.

V4-17.05.section_title: Entities, reference resolution, and multilingual coverage
V4-17.05.text: Original language and bytes MUST be preserved; translations are derived views with independent producer and uncertainty metadata.

V4-17.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-17.06.section_title: Entities, reference resolution, and multilingual coverage
V4-17.06.text: Cross-language retrieval MUST use tested multilingual artifacts or explicit translation policy; unsupported languages report reduced coverage.

V4-17.07.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/api_v3/facade.py, verbatim/retrieval/candidates.py; no mapped executable check
V4-17.07.section_title: Entities, reference resolution, and multilingual coverage
V4-17.07.text: Segmentation, tokenization, morphology, aliases, time expressions, and negation MUST be tested independently for each advertised language.

V4-17.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-17.08.section_title: Entities, reference resolution, and multilingual coverage
V4-17.08.text: Identity merge/split MUST invalidate dependent profiles, observations, caches, and indexes while preserving evidence and historical attribution.

V4-18.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-18.01.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.01.text: Claims MUST retain immutable revisions with recorded-time bounds, valid-time intervals, uncertainty, modality, polarity, and evidence references.

V4-18.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-18.02.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.02.text: Current-state, past-state, known-at, and timeline queries MUST select revisions and ranking statistics consistent with their declared temporal semantics.

V4-18.03.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.03.text: Conditions MUST use a typed, bounded expression language with true, false, and unknown evaluation; missing context cannot become true.

V4-18.04.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.04.text: Supersession proposals MUST name predecessor, successor, shared subject/topic, transition evidence, expected versions, and producer identity.

V4-18.05.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.05.text: Hearsay, negation, hypotheticals, future intent, quoted instructions, and ambiguous reference MUST not trigger automatic retirement without supporting evidence.

V4-18.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-18.06.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.06.text: Conflict detection MUST preserve competing interpretations and contradictory evidence instead of selecting the newest or most confident model output.

V4-18.07.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.07.text: Applying correction or supersession MUST atomically update lifecycle, dependency invalidation, projections, receipts, and required recomputation.

V4-18.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-18.08.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.08.text: Automatic updates MUST be restricted to measured low-risk classes; high-impact changes require an explicit owner/reviewer decision.

V4-18.09.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.09.text: Historical reads MUST apply current access and deletion restrictions while preserving the requested historical knowledge state where still available.

V4-18.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-18.10.section_title: Bitemporal claims, conditions, conflicts, and correction
V4-18.10.text: Update tests MUST include natural-language near misses and adversarial twins, not only templates matching the detector's regular expressions.

V4-19.01.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/storage/schema_v4.py; no mapped executable check
V4-19.01.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.01.text: A derivation edge MUST bind child revision, exact parent revision, producer manifest, operation receipt, scope, and creation sequence.

V4-19.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-19.02.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.02.text: Edge endpoints MUST exist in the object registry; scope compatibility and parent retention constraints MUST validate in the creation transaction.

V4-19.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-19.03.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.03.text: Derived objects MUST not become visible until their complete parent set and policy inheritance are durable.

V4-19.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-19.04.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.04.text: Evidence-family deduplication MUST track copying, common origin, and generated descendants without assuming unrelated identifiers imply independent testimony.

V4-19.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-19.05.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.05.text: Proof counts MUST mean counted evidence families under a named method, not statistically independent witnesses or verified truth.

V4-19.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-19.06.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.06.text: A derivative MUST never corroborate its own ancestors; cycles and self-support MUST fail validation or remain non-evidentiary research artifacts.

V4-19.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-19.07.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.07.text: Bounded ancestry traversal MUST return a complete result or an explicit continuation/incomplete status; silent depth or node truncation is prohibited.

V4-19.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-19.08.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.08.text: Correction, quarantine, revocation, and purge MUST invalidate all affected descendants through this same graph and registered side references.

V4-19.09.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/jobs/coordinator.py, verbatim/privacy/closure.py, verbatim/profiles/schema.py; no mapped executable check
V4-19.09.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.09.text: Every new object kind MUST register its access resolver, provenance rules, serializer, invalidator, eraser, and integrity checks before persistence.

V4-19.10.section_title: Provenance graph, independence, and truth dimensions
V4-19.10.text: User feedback MUST not rewrite provenance or collapse reliability, relevance, and authorization into a single trust score.

V4-20.01.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.01.text: Synthesis MUST be opt-in per scope and producer; enabling it MUST not enable remote dispatch, sharing, or sensitive inference.

V4-20.02.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.02.text: A generated view MUST record model/artifact identity, prompt/rubric revision, input refs, output digest, generation parameters, and policy epochs.

V4-20.03.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/storage/schema_v4.py, verbatim/synthesis/synthesizer.py, verbatim/synthesis/types.py; no mapped executable check
V4-20.03.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.03.text: Every externally delivered proposition MUST carry support mappings to accepted evidence or an explicit hypothesis/unsupported designation.

V4-20.04.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.04.text: Citation syntax, exact slice validity, and ancestry MUST be checked deterministically; semantic entailment remains a measured probabilistic judgment.

V4-20.05.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.05.text: Unsupported generated propositions MUST be excluded from factual answer-support packs and cannot become corroborating evidence for future synthesis.

V4-20.06.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.06.text: Generated output MUST be screened independently of its inputs and inherit the strictest contributing privacy, audience, purpose, and retention constraints.

V4-20.07.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.07.text: Invalidation of any required parent MUST immediately suppress the view pending recomputation; stale text cannot remain visible behind an old cache.

V4-20.08.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/synthesis/synthesizer.py; no mapped executable check
V4-20.08.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.08.text: Synthesis failure MUST preserve canonical evidence and return a typed unavailable/abstained result, not a partly validated generated memory.

V4-20.09.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/synthesis/synthesizer.py; no mapped executable check
V4-20.09.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.09.text: Generation logs MUST retain concise structured provenance, not private reasoning traces or raw prompts by default.

V4-20.10.section_title: Optional grounded synthesis and derived views
V4-20.10.text: Local and remote synthesis MUST pass the same grounding, deletion, and negative-transfer suites; model availability is not recommendation evidence.

V4-21.01.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/profiles/schema.py, verbatim/profiles/service.py, verbatim/profiles/types.py; no mapped executable check
V4-21.01.text: Profile schemas MUST support configurable topics, multiplicity, sensitivity, expiry, preferred evidence classes, and conflict handling.

V4-21.02.text: Explicit preferences MUST remain distinguishable from inferred preferences and temporary task constraints.

V4-21.03.text: Perspective records MUST separately represent asserter, observer, subject, and audience; default retrieval cannot bypass audience restrictions.

V4-21.04.text: Sensitive trait inference MUST default off and require explicit permitted purpose and owner policy; absence of a detector match is not consent.

V4-21.05.text: A profile update MUST identify changed fields, supporting/contradicting evidence, effective time, and the previous revision.

V4-21.06.text: Context selection MUST balance stable profile and recent relevant events within the final serialized budget, including formatting and provenance.

V4-21.07.text: Owners MUST be able to inspect, correct, disable inference for, and delete individual profile topics with complete derivative invalidation.

V4-21.08.text: Group sessions MUST not merge participants' preferences or expose one peer's private model to another without explicit authority.

V4-21.09.text: Personalization quality MUST measure beneficial adaptation, incorrect assumption rate, and user correction burden rather than profile size.

V4-21.10.text: Sharing a profile MUST not transfer source grants or reveal hidden supporting evidence identifiers to unauthorized recipients.

V4-22.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-22.01.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.01.text: Trajectories MUST record ordered actions, observations, tool invocation IDs, environment anchors, recovery attempts, and terminal disposition.

V4-22.02.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/experience/scenes.py; no mapped executable check
V4-22.02.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.02.text: Episode boundaries MUST name their rule or host event; inferred boundaries remain revisable with membership history.

V4-22.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-22.03.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.03.text: Episode outcomes MUST derive only from verified checker receipts or remain explicitly unknown/self-reported.

V4-22.04.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.04.text: Failed, abandoned, and partially successful episodes MUST be retained under policy as negative experience rather than omitted from learning.

V4-22.05.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.05.text: Scene membership MUST be revisioned and evidence-linked; similarity-based clustering cannot broaden audiences or erase conflicting episodes.

V4-22.06.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.06.text: Hierarchical summaries MUST preserve pointers to detailed evidence, contradictory branches, temporal bounds, and missing coverage.

V4-22.07.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.07.text: Retrieval MUST support exact episode lookup, task-family search, temporal sequence, and progressive scene-to-episode-to-span expansion.

V4-22.08.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.08.text: Parent scores MUST not establish child relevance; every delivered child passes query relevance and eligibility checks independently.

V4-22.09.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.09.text: Hierarchy construction MUST be incremental, bounded, and resumable rather than rescanning all history after each turn.

V4-22.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-22.10.section_title: Episodes, scenes, trajectories, and hierarchical memory
V4-22.10.text: Episode and scene benefits MUST be measured against flat retrieval on long-history and multi-hop workloads at equal total budgets.

V4-23.01.text: Checker receipts MUST bind a trusted issuer, invocation/task ID, environment digest, output artifact digest, completion status, nonce, and timestamp.

V4-23.02.text: A model-supplied checker name or exit code MUST remain an agent report; only a registered host resolver can attest execution.

V4-23.03.text: Procedures MUST encode ordered operations, bindings, prerequisites, applicability, verification steps, hazards, failure modes, and evidence revisions.

V4-23.04.text: Generated lessons MAY suggest abstractions or hypotheses, but MUST not invent successful execution or silently promote inferred preconditions to facts.

V4-23.05.text: Candidate, reviewed, trialed, recommended, and retired states MUST have separate promotion criteria and immutable review records.

V4-23.06.text: Reuse MUST rebind paths, versions, permissions, tool schemas, and environment anchors; stale or incompatible bindings block applicable recommendations.

V4-23.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-23.07.text: Contrastive refinement MUST compare relevant success and failure episodes without treating unobserved counterfactual outcomes as measured evidence.

V4-23.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-23.08.text: Exposure, adoption, execution, verified success, and verified failure MUST be counted separately with attribution to procedure revision.

V4-23.09.text: Automatic recommendation MUST pass held-out task-family tests; automatic promotion remains research until independent safety and utility gates pass.

V4-23.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-23.10.text: Exported skills MUST preserve provenance, hazards, applicability, and review state; executable installation requires separate host authorization.

V4-24.01.text: Consolidation MUST trigger from changed dependencies, recurrence, or explicit requests rather than every read or unconditional whole-store scans.

V4-24.02.text: Each job MUST state its input window, target object kinds, input/output budgets, retention policy, and expected generation.

V4-24.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-24.03.text: Corroboration MUST deduplicate shared origin and self-derived evidence; paraphrased copies cannot manufacture independent support.

V4-24.04.text: Rival values MUST remain separate alternatives linked to their support; averaging contradictory facts into one assertion is prohibited.

V4-24.05.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/observations/consolidate.py; no mapped executable check
V4-24.05.text: Compaction MUST preserve exact commands, identifiers, constraints, negations, safety warnings, and unresolved conflict closure.

V4-24.06.text: Reflection MUST produce labeled hypotheses or grounded views, never modify grants, trust attribution, checker receipts, or canonical source bytes.

V4-24.07.text: Refinement MUST create a new derivative revision and record why it replaced or supplemented the previous view.

V4-24.08.text: Unchanged inputs MUST not produce duplicate derivatives, unbounded job churn, or repeated remote billing.

V4-24.09.text: Consolidation MUST stop or back off when its utility gain is absent, review burden grows, or its allocated duty cycle is exhausted.

V4-24.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-24.10.text: Recomputing after deletion MUST not reconstruct erased content from stale summaries, prompts, caches, or alternative copies inside the authority boundary.

V4-25.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-25.01.text: Working sets MUST bind to caller/session/task and expire under an explicit policy; their contents pass ordinary disclosure and deletion checks.

V4-25.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-25.02.text: Plans and commitments MUST record owner, status, due-time precision, timezone, recurrence rule, evidence, and cancellation history.

V4-25.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-25.03.text: The engine MUST not execute reminders or actions merely because a plan became due; hosts opt into separately authorized delivery mechanisms.

V4-25.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-25.04.text: Environment observations MUST retain repository revision, tool versions, platform, configuration digest, and observation time where available.

V4-25.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-25.05.text: Freshness classes MUST distinguish stable, volatile, revalidate-after, stale, and unknown; unknown is never presented as verified current.

V4-25.06.text: Consequential-action contexts MUST request revalidation of volatile or expired dependencies before applicable procedure recommendations.

V4-25.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-25.07.text: Session summaries MUST not replace still-required exact instructions, safety constraints, or unresolved task state during context compression.

V4-25.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-25.08.text: Promotion from working to durable memory MUST require its own retention, evidence, and admission decisions.

V4-25.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-25.09.text: Decay MUST alter accessibility or relevance only; physical erasure requires the configured retention/destructive lifecycle policy.

V4-25.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-25.10.text: Wall-clock jumps, timezone changes, DST transitions, and replayed events MUST not silently duplicate commitments or expire the wrong records.

V4-26.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-26.01.text: Requests MUST contain a bound caller context, purpose, explicit scope narrowing, query, temporal semantics, requested kinds, and absolute budgets.

V4-26.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-26.02.text: Query limits MUST validate before private lookup: at most 8,192 characters, 32 KiB UTF-8, eight explicit entities, and 32 groups.

V4-26.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-26.03.text: Recall defaults MUST be eight groups, 6,000 serialized bytes, a 1,536-token target, and a 200 ms cooperative deadline.

V4-26.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-26.04.text: Explicit recall limits MUST remain within 512–24,000 bytes and 20–2,000 ms; richer reflection uses a separate request contract.

V4-26.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-26.05.text: Empty requested-kind sets MUST mean no kinds; omitted sets use documented defaults, and adapters MUST preserve that distinction.

V4-26.06.text: `min_ready` MUST reference capture receipts or projection watermarks for requested capabilities, not merely the latest event sequence.

V4-26.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-26.07.text: Results MUST report abstention, incomplete coverage, processing pending, omitted groups, capability outcomes, provenance, and delivery receipt.

V4-26.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-26.08.text: Hard identifier constraints MUST be applied to each supporting group, not satisfied by an unrelated authorized document elsewhere in the corpus.

V4-26.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-26.09.text: Inspect/explain endpoints MUST obey the same caller, purpose, and quote restrictions as recall, including metadata and ancestry disclosure.

V4-26.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-26.10.text: Wire versions MUST define unknown-field handling, enum evolution, null/empty semantics, and transport-safe typed errors.

V4-27.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-27.01.text: The production default controller MUST be deterministic, inspectable, versioned, and reproducible from recorded non-content state.

V4-27.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-27.02.text: Route selection MUST never broaden scopes, purposes, output kinds, disclosure consent, or budgets supplied by the caller.

V4-27.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-27.03.text: A route MUST distinguish missing evidence from incomplete search, index lag, unsupported language, and inference unavailability.

V4-27.04.text: Escalation MUST debit all retrieval, model, tool, and serialization work against one absolute request budget.

V4-27.05.text: Reflection MUST use allowlisted read-only memory operations; arbitrary shell, filesystem, connector, or browser access is outside the memory controller.

V4-27.06.text: Default reflection MUST allow at most three retrieval rounds and a 30-second deadline; expansion requires an explicit bounded request, maximum 120 seconds.

V4-27.07.text: Concurrent lanes MUST use supported snapshot semantics and independent connections where required; sequential execution must be reported as sequential.

V4-27.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-27.08.text: Learned routing MUST remain shadow-only until a frozen artifact wins held-out utility/resource gates without safety regression.

V4-27.09.text: Every omitted or skipped lane MUST record its reason; a deadline-skipped lane cannot report healthy completed coverage.

V4-27.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-27.10.text: The no-memory route MUST remain eligible when expected utility is low or dependencies are unsafe.

V4-28.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-28.01.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.01.text: Each lane MUST consume an `EligibilitySet` bound to scope, purpose, lifecycle, time, quarantine, retention, and epoch constraints.

V4-28.02.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.02.text: Top-k truncation MUST occur after eligibility; paging MUST continue through ineligible rows until the eligible bound or deadline is reached.

V4-28.03.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.03.text: BM25 document frequency, corpus size, and average length MUST reflect only the eligible authorization-equivalent corpus for that query.

V4-28.04.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.04.text: A shared FTS MATCH index MAY generate identifiers, but global FTS5 BM25 scores MUST NOT rank strict-isolation results.

V4-28.05.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/embeddings/vectors.py, verbatim/retrieval/candidates.py; no mapped executable check
V4-28.05.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.05.text: Authorized term statistics MUST use scoped postings or exact local counts with epoch-keyed caches; partial computation reports incomplete coverage.

V4-28.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-28.06.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.06.text: Entity composition MUST support exact intersection, union, exclusion, and relation predicates over authorized records without approximate algebraic guesses.

V4-28.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-28.07.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.07.text: Identifier search MUST preserve case-sensitive identifiers where meaningful, punctuation, namespaces, paths, versions, and exact quoted strings.

V4-28.08.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.08.text: Temporal lanes MUST apply known-at and valid-time constraints before scoring and prevent future records from changing historical ordering.

V4-28.09.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/retrieval/v3/lanes.py; no mapped executable check
V4-28.09.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.09.text: FTS corruption MAY degrade to an explicit bounded scan through the kernel; it MUST not hide integrity failures or claim complete coverage.

V4-28.10.section_title: Lexical, identifier, structured, and temporal retrieval
V4-28.10.text: Metamorphic tests MUST show unauthorized additions, deletions, and frequency changes leave authorized deterministic results unchanged.

V4-29.01.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.01.text: M1 MUST ship and measure one licensed, pinned local neural encoder through an explicitly installed, reviewed inference runtime; M0 must remain installable and qualified without it.

V4-29.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-29.02.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.02.text: Artifact identity MUST cover model bytes, tokenizer, preprocessing, normalization, dimension, quantization, runtime compatibility, and license provenance.

V4-29.03.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.03.text: Provider/model names containing valid namespace characters MUST remain valid descriptors; internal identifiers MUST use stable encoded identities rather than restrictive raw-name regexes.

V4-29.04.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.04.text: Exact cosine search MUST stream bounded batches of eligible vectors and maintain a bounded heap, without rejecting the entire corpus at a batch-size limit.

V4-29.05.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.05.text: Query and document vectors MUST share the same embedding space; stale input digests or mismatched generations MUST be excluded and reported.

V4-29.06.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.06.text: Deadline-limited scans MUST report scanned/eligible coverage and partial status; exact-search claims apply only to completed eligible scans.

V4-29.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-29.07.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.07.text: ANN MUST operate over authorization-compatible projections or use an exact filtered fallback; arbitrary post-filter oversampling is not an isolation proof.

V4-29.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-29.08.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.08.text: Neural models MUST never download on import or first recall; provisioning verifies hashes, license, disk/RAM requirements, and network policy explicitly.

V4-29.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-29.09.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.09.text: Sparse and late-interaction lanes MUST remain research until their artifacts, scorer, lifecycle, erasure, and ablation evidence exist.

V4-29.10.section_title: Neural retrieval, streaming exact search, and scalable indexes
V4-29.10.text: Remote query and document encoding MUST use §12 permits even when a configured encoder object already exists.

V4-30.01.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.01.text: Public entity probe and compositional query operations MUST have deterministic authorized SQL/reference implementations.

V4-30.02.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.02.text: A graph lane MUST seed from eligible relevant objects, validate every traversed node/edge, and bound examined edges, depth, and elapsed time.

V4-30.03.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.03.text: Relation labels MUST distinguish observed sequence, explicit causal assertion, inferred causal hypothesis, contradiction, and topic association.

V4-30.04.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.04.text: HRR research MUST pin atom encoding, roles, dimensions, numeric format, normalization, binding operations, and index generation.

V4-30.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-30.05.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.05.text: HRR MUST return candidate identifiers resolved through the kernel; decoding a plausible vector cannot mint a fact or evidence string.

V4-30.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-30.06.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.06.text: Capacity/noise tests MUST vary bundled item count, dimensionality, collisions, entity ambiguity, deletion, and adversarial distractors.

V4-30.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-30.07.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.07.text: HRR and graph deletion MUST remove or rebuild every affected aggregate; subtracting an approximate contribution without validation is insufficient.

V4-30.08.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/retrieval/v3/lanes.py; no mapped executable check
V4-30.08.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.08.text: Positive feedback MUST not make a candidate bypass evidence, relevance, freshness, or trust restrictions.

V4-30.09.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.09.text: Default graph expansion MUST be one hop with at most 100 visited nodes and 200 examined edges; expanded budgets remain explicit.

V4-30.10.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/retrieval/v3/lanes.py; no mapped executable check
V4-30.10.section_title: Associative graph retrieval and Holographic-style composition
V4-30.10.text: HRR becomes recommended only if it improves utility, latency, or memory footprint over exact composition plus hybrid retrieval without safety loss.

V4-31.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-31.01.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.01.text: Fusion MUST operate only on eligible candidates with stable object/revision identities and complete mandatory dependency groups.

V4-31.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-31.02.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.02.text: Reciprocal-rank fusion MUST be the transparent reference; learned scores require calibrated held-out benefit and stable fallbacks.

V4-31.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-31.03.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.03.text: Rerankers MUST score authorized text only, preserve exact identifiers and temporal constraints, and remain within request and egress budgets.

V4-31.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-31.04.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.04.text: Diversity MUST reduce redundant evidence without removing independent contrary evidence or necessary context members.

V4-31.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-31.05.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.05.text: Support verdicts MUST be per group: supported, partial, insufficient, conflicting, or verification-required, with separate reason codes.

V4-31.06.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.06.text: Neural paraphrase matches MUST be evaluated with semantic calibration; a fixed content-word overlap floor cannot be the universal support test.

V4-31.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-31.07.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.07.text: Hard-identifier absence MUST be distinguished from incomplete search; only complete eligible coverage justifies a confident absence claim.

V4-31.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-31.08.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.08.text: Thresholds MUST be calibrated by task class and language on development data, then frozen for held-out evaluation.

V4-31.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-31.09.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.09.text: Score explanations MUST expose signal categories and authorized evidence, not hidden chain-of-thought or inaccessible corpus statistics.

V4-31.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-31.10.section_title: Fusion, reranking, diversity, and calibrated abstention
V4-31.10.text: OOD, ambiguity, conflict, stale state, and denied access MUST remain distinguishable internally without leaking private existence to unauthorized callers.

V4-32.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-32.01.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.01.text: Pack kinds MUST include evidence, conflicts, profiles, working state, procedures, verification, and explicitly generated synthesis.

V4-32.02.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.02.text: Packing MUST treat each claim/context/conflict group atomically; screening or budget omission of a required member omits the whole group.

V4-32.03.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.03.text: Serialized byte ceilings MUST be checked on the final transport payload; token ceilings require a pinned tokenizer or a conservative declared bound.

V4-32.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-32.04.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.04.text: Bytes-divided-by-four MAY be reported as an estimate, but MUST NOT be called a guaranteed token ceiling.

V4-32.05.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.05.text: Progressive levels MUST expose a short navigational view, a grounded overview, and exact-detail expansion under separate authorization checks.

V4-32.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-32.06.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.06.text: Generated compression MUST retain support mappings and preserve identifiers, commands, conditions, negations, hazards, and contradictory alternatives.

V4-32.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-32.07.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.07.text: Evidence wrappers MUST label content as untrusted data; labels are advisory to the model and do not replace host execution policy.

V4-32.08.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.08.text: Screened output MUST be repacked and revalidated atomically; per-item removal cannot leave a misleading half-conflict or stripped condition.

V4-32.09.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.09.text: Expansion handles MUST be caller-, scope-, purpose-, revision-, and expiry-bound; they must not reveal hidden descendants or survive revocation.

V4-32.10.section_title: Context packs, progressive disclosure, and compression
V4-32.10.text: The same serializer and budget checker MUST serve API, MCP, SDK, cache, fallback lane, workbench export, and service responses.

V4-33.01.text: Cache keys MUST include caller authorization class, scope narrowing, purpose, output verbs, temporal semantics, requested kinds, policy revision, and dependency epochs.

V4-33.02.text: Cached objects MUST store validated references or protected payloads; every delivery requires fresh kernel validation and a new delivery permit.

V4-33.03.text: Correction, quarantine, revocation, erasure, artifact change, and index-generation change MUST invalidate all affected cache entries.

V4-33.04.text: Fuzzy/semantic caching MUST be disabled for exact identifiers, current-state changes, conflicting evidence, and unsupported semantic-equivalence cases.

V4-33.05.text: Prefetch MUST respect the host's query visibility, consent, deadlines, and cancellation; it cannot authorize remote processing preemptively.

V4-33.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-33.06.text: Raw query retention MUST default off; keyed fingerprints and minimized metadata are preferred where replay does not require exact inputs.

V4-33.07.text: Cache hit rates MUST be reported beside stale-hit, incorrect-reuse, invalidation, and privacy-fence metrics.

V4-33.08.text: Tenant-specific cache activity MUST not affect another tenant's exposed scores or diagnostics; shared-resource timing remains a declared threat-model limit.

V4-34.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-34.01.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.01.text: Every delivered item MUST have a handle linking caller, purpose, object revision, pack, policy epochs, and delivery receipt.

V4-34.02.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.02.text: Feedback MUST distinguish exposure, adoption, user helpfulness, verified outcome, and inferred relevance; missing feedback means unknown.

V4-34.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-34.03.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.03.text: Feedback writes MUST authorize the caller and bind to a real prior delivery; arbitrary IDs cannot alter another principal's ranking state.

V4-34.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-34.04.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.04.text: Replay MUST pin authorized input snapshots, policy/artifact manifests, budgets, and retained query inputs or report the unavailable stages honestly.

V4-34.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-34.05.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.05.text: Paired replay arms MUST start from identical snapshots and execute real production paths with isolated effects and equal caller authority.

V4-34.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-34.06.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.06.text: Erased or expired inputs MUST not be restored for replay; deletion includes sandbox copies and saved model inputs within the enumerated boundary.

V4-34.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-34.07.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.07.text: Learned changes MUST train on development data and pass separate held-out task-family gates before shadow or active deployment.

V4-34.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-34.08.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.08.text: A rollback report MUST identify impacted sessions, derivatives, and disclosures while stating which external actions or already delivered bytes cannot be undone.

V4-34.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-34.09.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.09.text: Online optimization MUST be bounded by a kill switch, exploration budget, and deterministic fallback that preserves every safety invariant.

V4-34.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-34.10.section_title: Influence, feedback, replay, and controlled improvement
V4-34.10.text: Influence records MUST use content-minimized identifiers and retention policy; an audit trail cannot become an undeletable copy of private memory.

V4-35.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-35.01.text: The threat model MUST include hostile documents, compromised connectors, malicious co-tenants, confused deputies, model-generated instructions, stale workers, and corrupted storage.

V4-35.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-35.02.text: In-scope attacks MUST include poisoning, delayed activation, compositional injection, provenance laundering, cross-scope inference, deletion evasion, replay, and resource exhaustion.

V4-35.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-35.03.text: The engine MUST enforce authorization, byte integrity, retention, suppression, dispatch permits, and budgets independently of model judgment.

V4-35.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-35.04.text: Content classifiers and generated support judgments MUST be evaluated probabilistically; no-findings labels cannot mean certified safety.

V4-35.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
