V4-35.05.text: Hosts MUST independently enforce tool permissions and sandboxing; recalled instructions and action tickets never supersede host policy.

V4-35.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-35.06.text: A compromised OS, unrestricted same-user process, or malicious in-process plugin is outside the embedded isolation guarantee and must be stated prominently.

V4-35.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-35.07.text: Database contents, WAL, caches, temporary files, logs, exports, model inputs, and backup key copies MUST appear in the asset inventory.

V4-35.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-35.08.text: Shared-hardware timing side channels MUST be distinguished from preventable application-level score, count, identifier, and error leaks.

V4-35.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-35.09.text: Each deployment profile MUST have a tested exposure matrix; stdio assumptions cannot justify an unauthenticated HTTP deployment.

V4-35.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-35.10.text: Security documentation MUST state residual risk, known exclusions, test populations, and the date of the last independent review.

V4-36.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-36.01.text: Screening MUST run on capture, interpretation, derivative creation, promotion, retrieval, and assembled delivery as applicable.

V4-36.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-36.02.text: Content form, attack findings, origin trust, review state, and sensitivity MUST remain separate fields.

V4-36.03.text: Quarantine on a source, accepted view, span, interpretation, or derivative MUST immediately exclude every dependent delivery and producer input.

V4-36.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-36.04.text: Quarantine release MUST be an authorized scoped decision with reasons and history; it cannot relabel external content as human or host-authenticated.

V4-36.05.text: Group-level screening MUST inspect combined deliverable content and delimiters; secret regexes alone do not implement compositional injection defense.

V4-36.06.text: The same hold cascade MUST apply to raw browsing, fallback scans, exports, sharing, cached packs, embeddings, and file projection.

V4-36.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-36.07.text: Suspicious write bursts, identity changes, repeated correction attempts, and synthetic corroboration MUST produce auditable anomaly signals without automatic guilt assumptions.

V4-36.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-36.08.text: Rollback MUST retain implicated source holds so recomputation cannot recreate poisoned derivatives from unchanged inputs.

V4-36.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-36.09.text: Defensive testing MUST use synthetic canaries and isolated sinks; no test may exfiltrate real credentials or execute destructive payloads.

V4-36.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-36.10.text: Attack success and benign retained coverage MUST be reported per lifecycle stage, language, source channel, and profile.

V4-37.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-37.01.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.01.text: Sensitivity classes MUST distinguish public, internal, personal, restricted, and secret values with explicit per-class handling policy.

V4-37.02.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.02.text: Detected/declared restricted values MUST be rejected or retained only in authenticated encryption before ordinary indexing, logging, or synthesis.

V4-37.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-37.03.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.03.text: Sanitized views MUST retain protected locators to encrypted originals; redaction text cannot be mistaken for original source bytes.

V4-37.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-37.04.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.04.text: Vault entries MUST use reviewed AEAD, authenticated scope/object metadata, per-entry data keys, and owner-approved wrapping-key providers.

V4-37.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-37.05.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.05.text: Hydration MUST require purpose, recipient, current grant, distinct consent, task need, freshness where applicable, and a one-use bounded handle.

V4-37.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-37.06.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.06.text: Exact-value disclosure to a task tool MUST be separate from consent to send context to an enrichment model.

V4-37.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-37.07.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.07.text: Action tickets MUST bind an exact action digest, gateway, recipient, caller, purpose, dependencies, expiry, and one-use nonce.

V4-37.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-37.08.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.08.text: Tickets MUST default to 30 seconds and never exceed 60 seconds; gateways recheck current policy and independent tool permission before execution.

V4-37.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-37.09.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.09.text: Without a cooperating gateway, status MUST report `action_use_enforcement=advisory_only`; context labels cannot claim action prevention.

V4-37.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-37.10.section_title: Sensitive values, encrypted vault, hydration, and action tickets
V4-37.10.text: Vault erasure reports MUST distinguish logical inaccessibility from externally verified destruction of every decrypting key copy.

V4-38.01.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.01.text: Suppression MUST atomically tombstone target roots and advance visibility epochs before any asynchronous cleanup is acknowledged.

V4-38.02.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.02.text: Descendants MUST be excluded immediately by current ancestry/epoch checks, even before a large closure has been enumerated.

V4-38.03.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.03.text: Physical cleanup MUST persist run identity, frontier, processed references, continuation cursors, and verification state in durable tables.

V4-38.04.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.04.text: Unprocessed dependency edges MUST remain discoverable; hitting a bound MUST yield pending continuation, never successful terminal deletion.

V4-38.05.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.05.text: Cleanup MUST cover sources, views, interpretations, derivatives, vectors, FTS, caches, projections, replay inputs, prompts, logs, and learned artifacts where attributable.

V4-38.06.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.06.text: Mixed-ancestry derivatives MUST be suppressed until recomputed from surviving authorized parents, not left readable with obsolete text.

V4-38.07.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.07.text: In-flight producers MUST revalidate erasure epochs during apply; deleted inputs cannot republish embeddings or regenerated summaries.

V4-38.08.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.08.text: Deletion receipts MUST enumerate verified surfaces, pending work, inaccessible external copies, cryptographic status, and residual backup obligations.

V4-38.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-38.09.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.09.text: Retention expiry MUST use the same closure path as explicit deletion; contentless tombstones retain only policy-approved replay-prevention metadata.

V4-38.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-38.10.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.10.text: Tombstone compaction MUST preserve enough deletion knowledge to reject old imports or replica resurrection within the declared retention horizon.

V4-38.11.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.11.text: Physical cleanup failure MUST retain suppression and retryable obligations; it cannot restore visibility to improve availability.

V4-38.12.section_title: Retention, forgetting, suppression, and deletion closure
V4-38.12.text: The 513-child regression MUST also be tested at 50,000 descendants, restart boundaries, shared parents, and foreign-scope dependencies.

V4-39.01.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.01.text: Key creation MUST use exclusive creation, complete writes, restrictive permissions, file fsync, and parent-directory durability before dependent commits.

V4-39.02.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.02.text: Missing or malformed existing keys MUST fail locked; silent regeneration or plaintext fallback is prohibited.

V4-39.03.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.03.text: Rotation MUST use versioned keys, resumable rewrap progress, concurrent-reader fencing, and explicit retirement of obsolete decrypting copies.

V4-39.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-39.04.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.04.text: Backup MUST use a consistent SQLite snapshot or service equivalent and include a manifest of schema, artifacts, key references, and erasure watermark.

V4-39.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-39.05.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.05.text: Recovery MUST restore key access separately from public artifacts; keys MUST NOT be placed in an unencrypted portable bundle beside ciphertext.

V4-39.06.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.06.text: Restore MUST reconcile current deletion knowledge before serving; an old backup without trusted newer erasure state reports unproven restoration safety.

V4-39.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-39.07.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.07.text: Whole-store encryption MUST be an explicitly provisioned reviewed backend; standard builds disclose plaintext-at-rest evidence outside the vault.

V4-39.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-39.08.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.08.text: Recovery drills MUST include process crash, interrupted rotation, disk-full, missing key, corrupt key, stale backup, and damaged index.

V4-39.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-39.09.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.09.text: Cryptographic erasure claims MUST specify the key hierarchy, backup/replica boundary, destruction evidence, and remaining decryptable copies.

V4-39.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-39.10.section_title: Keys, backups, restore, and cryptographic recovery
V4-39.10.text: Health/status MUST expose locked, recovering, stale-erasure-state, and ready states without printing secret key material.

V4-40.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-40.01.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.01.text: SQLite deployments MUST use local supported filesystems, WAL, foreign keys, durable synchronization, and reviewed runtime builds.

V4-40.02.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.02.text: Writer admission MUST use a deadline-aware queue or timed lock; waiting cannot exceed the request's remaining budget.

V4-40.03.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.03.text: SQLite busy timeout MUST be bounded by the smaller of configured contention allowance and remaining operation time.

V4-40.04.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/storage/store.py; no mapped executable check
V4-40.04.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.04.text: Ordinary write batches MUST target at most 25 ms lock hold; oversized work MUST split at transaction-safe continuation boundaries.

V4-40.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-40.05.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.05.text: Recall MUST avoid synchronous analytics and learning writes; its required delivery receipt MUST remain minimal, with bounded group commit permitted.

V4-40.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-40.06.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.06.text: Read snapshots MUST be short and bounded; model inference and large external scans MUST not pin WAL checkpoints.

V4-40.07.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.07.text: WAL bytes, checkpoint progress, oldest reader age, write wait, and write hold MUST be measured and exposed through operator diagnostics.

V4-40.08.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.08.text: Maintenance MUST use staged generations and chunked work; a whole-store rebuild under one long writer lock is prohibited.

V4-40.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-40.09.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.09.text: Capacity decisions MUST measure claim/span/derivative counts, payload bytes, index size, active scopes, concurrency, and write amplification together.

V4-40.10.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.10.text: Saturation MUST return explicit backpressure or partial authorized results; dropping integrity checks to meet a latency target is prohibited.

V4-40.11.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-40.11.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.11.text: The system MUST reserve resources for suppression/revocation; if suppression cannot persist, it must not acknowledge success and must enter fail-closed service posture.

V4-40.12.section_title: SQLite concurrency, deadlines, WAL, and capacity
V4-40.12.text: Multiple processes MUST coordinate schema changes and worker ownership; an in-process mutex alone is not a cross-process protocol.

V4-41.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-41.01.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.01.text: The schema MUST enforce endpoint existence, uniqueness, immutable scope ownership, and revision consistency with database constraints where representable.

V4-41.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-41.02.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.02.text: JSON fields MUST have versioned validated schemas and bounded sizes; privacy-critical constraints cannot depend on unvalidated free-form JSON.

V4-41.03.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.03.text: Historical migration checksums MUST be verified against immutable migration definitions before mutation is permitted.

V4-41.04.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/core/types_v4.py, verbatim/storage/schema_v4.py; no mapped executable check
V4-41.04.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.04.text: Repair DDL and index changes MUST be versioned migration phases, not undocumented string-sniffing changes after schema-version advancement.

V4-41.05.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.05.text: A migration MUST advance the public schema version only after all required phases and integrity checks succeed.

V4-41.06.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.06.text: Resumable phases MUST persist cursor and validation state; non-resumable phases MUST roll back cleanly and report restart-from-zero honestly.

V4-41.07.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.07.text: Migration ownership MUST be rechecked after acquiring the cross-process lock, with explicit behavior for concurrent old/new binaries.

V4-41.08.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.08.text: Unknown newer schemas MUST refuse mutation; downgrades require a tested export/import path, not forced version-number edits.

V4-41.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-41.09.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.09.text: Integrity checks MUST cover graph endpoints, policy inheritance, receipts, readiness, indexes, and erasure frontier in addition to SQLite foreign keys.

V4-41.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-41.10.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.10.text: Schema review MUST include query plans and indexes for authority checks, closure traversal, queue leasing, and historical retrieval.

V4-41.11.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-41.11.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.11.text: Each milestone MUST migrate only the schema needed for its reachable capabilities, with immutable migration identifiers and no duplicate authoritative tables introduced for API-version convenience.

V4-41.12.section_title: Schema evolution for v4 and verifiable migrations
V4-41.12.text: Store reconciliation MUST inventory both Hermes database conventions, preserve provenance and scope, and require explicit destination/conflict approval; never choose the newest file as an implicit authority.

V4-42.01.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.01.text: Job leases MUST carry monotonically increasing fencing tokens verified inside the domain application transaction.

V4-42.02.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.02.text: Job identity MUST include operation digest, scope, input revisions, producer/config revision, and declared required capabilities.

V4-42.03.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.03.text: Cancellation, revocation, and erasure MUST fence both final publication and queued follow-up work; early read-time checks are insufficient.

V4-42.04.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.04.text: Privacy/control work MUST have reserved service capacity; weighted fairness MUST prevent indefinite starvation of capture or other scopes.

V4-42.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-42.05.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.05.text: Queue caps MUST include queued, leased, retrying, and background obligations with per-scope and global disk/resource bounds.

V4-42.06.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.06.text: Deduplicated retries MUST resolve existing obligations before applying new-item backpressure; a full queue cannot make receipt lookup non-idempotent.

V4-42.07.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.07.text: Retry policy MUST distinguish transient, permanent, capability-unavailable, cancelled, lease-lost, and operator-action-required failures.

V4-42.08.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.08.text: Expired leases MUST be reclaimed after restart; retries MUST preserve lineage and cannot vacate successful operation receipts.

V4-42.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-42.09.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.09.text: Long computation MAY renew a lease within policy, but renewal cannot exceed job deadline or override revocation.

V4-42.10.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.10.text: Handler success MUST mean required effects and continuation obligations are durable; truncated cleanup or skipped mandatory work cannot report success.

V4-42.11.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-42.11.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.11.text: Retained operational history MUST be bounded without deleting security-relevant receipts before their retention policy permits.

V4-42.12.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-42.12.section_title: Durable jobs, fairness, and crash semantics
V4-42.12.text: Crash tests MUST interrupt each boundary between lease, inference, domain apply, receipt, completion, and downstream enqueue.

V4-43.01.text: Every projection MUST record parent snapshot watermark, producer/artifact manifest, coverage, build state, and publication generation.

V4-43.02.text: Rebuild MUST write into a staging generation in bounded transactions while queries continue using the prior valid generation.

V4-43.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-43.03.text: Catch-up MUST replay intervening eligible changes and erasures before atomic compare-and-swap publication.

V4-43.04.text: Scope-partition rebuilds MUST not strand unrelated scopes behind a global generation bump.

V4-43.05.text: Resume MUST validate its checkpoint, artifact identity, and source watermark; incompatible partial artifacts are discarded safely and reported.

V4-43.06.text: Index corruption MUST never be treated as canonical evidence corruption unless the evidence checks fail independently.

V4-43.07.text: Historical coverage MUST state which revisions are indexed; current-only indexes cannot masquerade as complete known-at retrieval.

V4-43.08.text: Old generations MUST be reclaimed after reader leases expire, with memory/disk limits and no premature deletion under active readers.

V4-43.09.text: Deletion MUST suppress immediately across all generations and physically remove attributable entries from staging as well as active indexes.

V4-43.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-43.10.text: Settled pre/post-rebuild results MUST preserve eligibility and explain ranking changes; a rebuild cannot be required to heal ordinary approval visibility.

V4-44.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.01.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.01.text: The storage interface MUST preserve operation receipts, temporal semantics, grants, digest verification, closure, and delivery permits across backends.

V4-44.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.02.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.02.text: PostgreSQL support MUST use supported pinned server versions, explicit transaction isolation, bounded serialization retries, and parameterized queries.

V4-44.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.03.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.03.text: Concurrent workers MUST lease with row-level coordination and fencing; `SKIP LOCKED` alone does not make domain effects idempotent.

V4-44.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.04.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.04.text: Tenant isolation MUST be enforced by application authority and database roles/policies where applicable; connection pooling cannot retain another caller's context.

V4-44.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.05.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.05.text: Service caches, vector indexes, and search statistics MUST satisfy the same authorization-local isolation as the SQLite reference.

V4-44.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.06.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.06.text: Database/vector extensions MUST be reviewed, versioned, and optional; an external vector service cannot become an ungoverned evidence authority.

V4-44.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.07.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.07.text: Backup, failover, replication lag, region placement, and deletion propagation MUST have explicit recovery and consistency contracts.

V4-44.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.08.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.08.text: SQLite-to-service migration MUST use verified export/import, a cutover watermark, a frozen writer window, and rollback criteria; blind dual writes are prohibited.

V4-44.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.09.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.09.text: Cross-backend differential tests MUST compare authorized results, lifecycle transitions, failure classes, and erasure outcomes from identical operation streams.

V4-44.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-44.10.section_title: Optional service backend and multi-tenant scale
V4-44.10.text: `scaled_service` MUST remain unavailable until S4 mixed-load, isolation, restore, and cost gates pass on the actual backend.

V4-45.01.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.01.text: Public mutation APIs MUST require operation IDs and return durable receipts with accepted effects and readiness references.

V4-45.02.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.02.text: Model-visible tools MUST not mint principals, grants, endpoints, capture consent, verified checker receipts, or operator authority.

V4-45.03.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.03.text: Fresh-store ownership and retention consent MUST be established by an explicit trusted setup flow, not arbitrary model-supplied scope names.

V4-45.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-45.04.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.04.text: MCP tools MUST expose capture, recall, context, inspect, correction proposal, feedback, readiness, and capabilities; reflection requires separate enablement.

V4-45.05.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.05.text: Destructive deletion, grant changes, quarantine release, and promotion MUST require operator-bound tools or an authenticated confirmation workflow.

V4-45.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-45.06.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.06.text: HTTP MUST validate issuer, audience, expiry, resource, scope, and replay protections; CORS and CSRF policy MUST match the client model.

V4-45.07.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.07.text: All transports MUST enforce input bounds, duplicate-key rejection, typed errors, cancellation, and final serialized output budgets.

V4-45.08.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.08.text: Service endpoints MUST default to loopback and explicit launch; a library import cannot create a listener.

V4-45.09.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.09.text: Schema conformance tests MUST include null/empty distinctions, unknown fields, enum evolution, invalid UTF-8, and unauthorized identifier probing.

V4-45.10.section_title: Public API, SDKs, MCP, and HTTP transport
V4-45.10.text: Compatibility aliases MUST route to v4 services or fail explicitly; old unsafe fallback behavior cannot be preserved as compatibility.

V4-46.01.text: M0 MUST qualify actual Hermes plugin discovery and lifecycle; M3 adds live ADK and cross-host task reuse, using disposable stores and separately authorized host installations.

V4-46.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-46.02.text: Every adapter MUST publish compatible host versions, supported hooks, missing hooks, drain ownership, and failure behavior.

V4-46.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-46.03.text: Caller identity and scope MUST be host-bound; request text or model arguments cannot override them.

V4-46.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-46.04.text: Tool outcomes MUST resolve through actual host invocation records rather than user-supplied checker labels.

V4-46.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-46.05.text: Capture MUST handle retries, forks, resumes, duplicate event delivery, session cancellation, and host shutdown without attribution drift.

V4-46.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-46.06.text: Prefetch MUST not mutate delivered history, tool schemas, or system prompts; hosts decide how authorized memory enters context.

V4-46.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-46.07.text: Provider failure MUST leave host operation usable with explicit degraded status, without swallowing accepted-work obligations.

V4-46.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-46.08.text: Installation MUST not activate a provider, migrate live history, or change host configuration without explicit owner approval.

V4-46.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-46.09.text: Optional adapter dependencies MUST not import into the core engine or increase the default installation's network surface.

V4-46.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-46.10.text: A generic MCP connection MUST not be advertised as full native capture, checker attestation, or cross-host task reuse.

V4-47.01.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.01.text: Markdown projections MUST include stable object references, revision, view kind, provenance links, and permitted edit semantics.

V4-47.02.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/projections/bundle.py; no mapped executable check
V4-47.02.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.02.text: Export MUST authorize every included object and dependency; hidden sources cannot leak through titles, paths, summaries, or link targets.

V4-47.03.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.03.text: Import MUST validate bundle manifests, signatures where present, digests, size bounds, path containment, and current deletion policy.

V4-47.04.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.04.text: Foreign signatures prove origin under a key, not local authority; imported grants and checker claims require explicit trust mapping.

V4-47.05.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/projections/__init__.py, verbatim/projections/edits.py; no mapped executable check
V4-47.05.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.05.text: File changes MUST become new source/derivative revisions with conflict detection and review; generated text cannot overwrite original evidence.

V4-47.06.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.06.text: Projection roots MUST reject symlink escapes, path traversal, executable hooks, and unexpected external fetches.

V4-47.07.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.07.text: Handoff capsules MUST bind recipient, purpose, expiry, object revisions, and allowed operations; they cannot delegate more authority than their issuer.

V4-47.08.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.08.text: Offline handoff MUST report unknown current revocation and use explicit short cached-authorization leases; offline act/hydrate/promotion is prohibited.

V4-47.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-47.09.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.09.text: Deletion MUST revoke tracked exports/projections and report unrevocable copies honestly; Git history is an external retention boundary, not erasure proof.

V4-47.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-47.10.section_title: File projections, portable bundles, and handoff
V4-47.10.text: Writable multi-device synchronization MUST remain separate from portable export/import until conflict and tombstone propagation gates pass.

V4-48.01.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/connectors/base.py, verbatim/connectors/service.py; no mapped executable check
V4-48.01.text: Importers MUST support structured exports from the named competitive registry where licensing and API access permit, with explicit per-provider coverage.

V4-48.02.text: Imported summaries or extracted facts without originals MUST be labeled imported assertions, never reconstructed as byte-exact original evidence.

V4-48.03.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/connectors/base.py, verbatim/connectors/service.py; no mapped executable check
V4-48.03.text: Dry-run import MUST report counts, scope mappings, missing provenance, sensitivity findings, duplicates, costs, and planned changes.

V4-48.04.text: Connector identity, cursor, source revision, retention policy, and permission snapshot MUST be recorded with each accepted batch.

V4-48.05.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/connectors/base.py, verbatim/connectors/handlers.py, verbatim/connectors/service.py; no mapped executable check
V4-48.05.text: Cursor advancement and accepted batch receipt MUST commit together; retries cannot skip or duplicate source changes silently.

V4-48.06.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/connectors/registry.py; no mapped executable check
V4-48.06.text: Remote fetchers MUST enforce endpoint allowlists, redirect limits, SSRF protection, content bounds, and separate source-access credentials.

V4-48.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-48.07.text: Upstream deletion or permission loss MUST create current suppression and closure obligations rather than leaving searchable stale copies.

V4-48.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-48.08.text: Reconciliation MUST distinguish source disappearance, temporary outage, permission denial, and explicit deletion before destructive action.

V4-48.09.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/connectors/handlers.py; no mapped executable check
V4-48.09.text: Bulk migration MUST be resumable and reversible before cutover; live provider switching always requires explicit operator approval.

V4-48.10.text: Interchange formats MUST preserve supported fields and report losses; unsupported semantic equivalence cannot be hidden behind a successful import count.

V4-49.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-49.01.text: Setup MUST explain capture, model installation, egress, storage encryption, and worker ownership before enabling any of them.

V4-49.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-49.02.text: The CLI MUST expose init, capture, recall, inspect, explain, correct, jobs, drain, status, doctor, export, import, migrate, and forget.

V4-49.03.note: implementation cites this id in verbatim/workbench/app.py; no mapped executable check
V4-49.03.text: Workbench views MUST show exact evidence beside interpretations and generated views, with distinct provenance and support labels.

V4-49.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-49.04.text: Review queues MUST prioritize risk and expected utility, support evidence comparison, and measure review burden rather than hide pending volume.

V4-49.05.text: Forget workflows MUST preview scope and closure, require appropriate confirmation, and display suppressed, cleaning, verified, and external-obligation states.

V4-49.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-49.06.text: Model setup MUST display license, artifact size, estimated resource envelope, network requirements, and alternatives without automatic downloads.

V4-49.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-49.07.text: Accessibility MUST include keyboard operation, readable contrast, non-color-only statuses, screen-reader labels, and copyable machine-readable receipts.

V4-49.08.text: Web workbench content MUST escape stored text and disable active HTML/scripts; evidence rendering cannot become an XSS channel.

V4-49.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-49.09.text: The local workbench MUST default to authenticated loopback or an equally reviewed local-session boundary; localhost alone is not sufficient web authorization.

V4-49.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-49.10.text: Onboarding tests MUST include novice users, clean installs, no-model operation, missing keys, unavailable inference, and recovery from a failed drain.

V4-50.01.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.01.text: Configuration MUST distinguish installed, configured, authorized, available, healthy, measured, and recommended states for every capability.

V4-50.02.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.02.text: A configured flag or importable NumPy MUST not imply a usable encoder, sparse scorer, index, key provider, or model artifact.

V4-50.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-50.03.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.03.text: Validation MUST reject unknown fields, duplicate keys, string booleans, bool-as-int, non-finite numbers, and incompatible profile/transport settings.

V4-50.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-50.04.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.04.text: Effective configuration MUST have a versioned digest; tightening policy advances epochs and invalidates disallowed work and permits.

V4-50.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-50.05.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.05.text: Model/judgment requests MUST carry task schema, allowed outputs, immutable input refs, deadlines, and producer/rubric identity.

V4-50.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-50.06.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.06.text: Advisory outputs MUST be bounded, schema-validated, calibrated where claimed, and independently checked before any domain application.

V4-50.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-50.07.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.07.text: Model uncertainty MUST not be conflated with correctness; provider confidence requires deployment-specific evaluation before threshold use.

V4-50.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-50.08.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.08.text: Missing advisory inference MUST preserve deterministic evidence operations and report the unavailable enhancement explicitly.

V4-50.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-50.09.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.09.text: Remote provider credentials MUST come from scoped secret accessors, never stored configuration values or ambient environment fallback inside transports.

V4-50.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-50.10.section_title: Configuration, runtime capabilities, and advisory decisions
V4-50.10.text: Default configuration MUST keep remote spend at zero, telemetry off, and all optional generation/promotion disabled.

V4-51.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-51.01.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.01.text: Traces MUST correlate capture, obligations, interpretation, index publication, recall, delivery, feedback, and deletion through content-minimized identifiers.

V4-51.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-51.02.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.02.text: Metrics MUST include accepted-to-ready latency, queue age, retries, dead letters, write wait/hold, WAL growth, and projection coverage.

V4-51.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-51.03.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.03.text: Retrieval metrics MUST include lane status, examined eligible objects, incomplete coverage, omitted groups, abstention, and final bytes/tokens.

V4-51.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-51.04.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.04.text: Learning metrics MUST include unsupported proposals, correction precision, review burden, stale views, verified procedure outcomes, and negative transfer.

V4-51.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-51.05.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.05.text: Egress metrics MUST include denied dispatches, reservations, timeouts, reconciliation, overruns, and recipient/purpose dimensions without payloads.

V4-51.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-51.06.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.06.text: Logs MUST redact credentials, private text, exact sensitive values, model prompts, and inaccessible identifiers by default.

V4-51.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-51.07.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.07.text: Operator diagnostics MUST be scope-authorized; cross-tenant aggregate dashboards require explicit administrative authority.

V4-51.08.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.08.text: Telemetry export MUST use the egress broker and opt-in policy; local observability must work with all network access disabled.

V4-51.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-51.09.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.09.text: Alert thresholds MUST be tied to declared SLOs and budgets, with runbooks for persistent readiness lag, erasure backlog, and writer saturation.

V4-51.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-51.10.section_title: Observability, service levels, and content-minimized audit
V4-51.10.text: Instrumentation MUST report its own overhead and dropped optional records; a broken audit sink cannot silently waive mandatory disclosure receipts.

V4-52.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-52.01.section_title: Error taxonomy, abuse resistance, and failure behavior
V4-52.01.text: Errors MUST have stable code, retryability, operation receipt where applicable, safe detail, and correlation ID.

V4-52.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-52.02.section_title: Error taxonomy, abuse resistance, and failure behavior
V4-52.02.text: Partial results MUST state completed stages and coverage; authorization/integrity failures never degrade into weaker content access.

V4-52.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-52.03.section_title: Error taxonomy, abuse resistance, and failure behavior
V4-52.03.text: Input limits MUST cover nesting, JSON size, regex work, entity lists, graph fan-out, decompression, and parser output.

V4-52.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-52.04.section_title: Error taxonomy, abuse resistance, and failure behavior
V4-52.04.text: Per-caller and per-scope quotas MUST bound accepted work, inference, search expansion, and retained operational history.

V4-52.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-52.05.section_title: Error taxonomy, abuse resistance, and failure behavior
V4-52.05.text: Circuit breakers MUST isolate failing optional backends while preserving local evidence access and mandatory privacy work.

V4-52.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-52.06.section_title: Error taxonomy, abuse resistance, and failure behavior
V4-52.06.text: Malformed optional results MUST be discarded without contaminating canonical records or leaking raw provider responses.

V4-52.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-52.07.section_title: Error taxonomy, abuse resistance, and failure behavior
V4-52.07.text: Disk-full and audit-write failure MUST not produce false capture, suppression, or delivery success receipts.

V4-52.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-52.08.section_title: Error taxonomy, abuse resistance, and failure behavior
V4-52.08.text: Error tests MUST include cancellation storms, retry storms, clock skew, transport disconnects, and concurrent policy changes.

V4-53.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.01.text: Every suite MUST pin dataset revision, licensing disposition, task IDs, splits, preprocessing, gold schema, and scoring implementation.

V4-53.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.02.text: Gold answers and expected evidence MUST be inaccessible to provider adapters, controllers, synthesis producers, and query rewriting.

V4-53.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.03.text: Corpora MUST include realistic distractors, changed facts, ambiguous entities, unrelated private scopes, stale state, and no-answer cases.

V4-53.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.04.text: The owned holdout MUST include at least 200 paired tasks across 20 task families and ten repositories/environments, with both required hosts represented.

V4-53.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.05.text: Train/development/test splits MUST separate users, source histories, repositories, and task families where leakage would otherwise occur.

V4-53.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.06.text: Benchmark-specific tuning MUST use development data only; a final locked holdout cannot become the next tuning corpus without a fresh replacement.

V4-53.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.07.text: Memory-control comparisons MUST execute identical task environments with the same reader, tools, permissions, and resource ceilings.

V4-53.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.08.text: Synthetic and template-generated cases MUST be reported separately from natural histories and independently authored adversarial cases.

V4-53.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.09.text: Missing licenses or access MUST block the affected run/claim, not trigger unauthorized download, redistribution, or a fabricated zero score.

V4-53.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-53.10.text: Corpus size MUST be reported in histories, questions, tokens, sources, spans, claims, and independent clusters rather than a single misleading count.

V4-54.01.text: Every competitor run MUST pin edition, commit/API version, deployment, models, prompts, extraction settings, retrieval budgets, readiness policy, and pricing date.

V4-54.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.02.text: Native-track comparisons MUST preserve each provider's documented strengths and record its actual total resource use.

V4-54.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.03.text: Controlled-track comparisons MUST share reader model, task environment, evidence access, context budget, and tuning allowance where technically possible.

V4-54.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.04.text: Hosted proprietary behavior MUST not be attributed to the OSS edition; self-hosted and managed results need separate rows.

V4-54.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.05.text: Comparator setup MUST use documented defaults plus a reasonable declared tuning track; disabled embeddings or broken ingestion cannot count as a competitor loss.

V4-54.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.06.text: Competitor failures MUST be diagnosed, recorded, and retried only under the preregistered policy; persistent unavailable runs remain unavailable.

V4-54.07.text: Total cost MUST include ingestion, extraction, embeddings, consolidation, query inference, answer reading, storage, and maintenance over declared amortization windows.

V4-54.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.08.text: Provider-native answer synthesis MUST be measured separately from evidence-only retrieval so an extra model call cannot masquerade as a retrieval improvement.

V4-54.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.09.text: Dataset/model/code license reviews MUST be independent; a repository license does not automatically license inherited data or third-party task environments.

V4-54.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.10.text: HaluMem's previously observed restrictive dataset terms and unresolved MemConflict redistribution permission MUST remain blockers until reviewed permission is established.

V4-54.11.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.11.text: No paid endpoint, production account, competitor migration, or private history may be used without separate explicit authorization.

V4-54.12.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.12.text: Comparator maintainers SHOULD receive reproducible configuration details and an opportunity to identify setup errors before public superiority claims.

V4-54.13.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-54.13.text: The v4.0 comparator set MUST include pinned Holographic, Mem0 OSS, Graphiti OSS, and current ReMe, plus no-memory, the previous stable VERBATIM, and simple lexical-plus-neural references; unavailable required comparators block comparison qualification rather than count as defeated.

V4-55.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.01.text: Reports MUST separate evidence recall/precision, answer correctness, supported-proposition rate, update errors, task success, and negative transfer.

V4-55.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.02.text: Paired comparisons MUST use cluster-aware bootstrap or an appropriate paired model at the user/history/repository/task-family independence level.

V4-55.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.03.text: Primary superiority claims MUST use simultaneous 95% intervals or preregistered multiplicity correction across named competitors and outcomes.

V4-55.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.04.text: Non-inferiority margins MUST be fixed before evaluation; a non-significant difference is not proof of equivalence.

V4-55.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.05.text: Zero observed failures MUST include denominators and confidence bounds; 460 template variants do not imply 460 independent natural-language trials.

V4-55.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.06.text: Rare-error gates MUST meet their stated upper confidence bound with sufficient independent samples; the rule of three is only an approximation under suitable assumptions.

V4-55.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.07.text: LLM judges MUST be blinded to provider identity, calibrated against human labels, and checked for position bias and judge-model sensitivity.

V4-55.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.08.text: Deterministic executable checks MUST score code/task artifacts when possible; model opinion cannot replace a failing test result.

V4-55.09.text: Latency reports MUST include p50/p95/p99, cold/warm runs, concurrency, timeout/error rates, and end-to-end readiness costs.

V4-55.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.10.text: Claims MUST publish uncertainty, negative results, per-category regressions, exact denominators, and unsupported capabilities beside averages.

V4-55.11.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.11.text: Leader selection MUST not tune against the final holdout; strongest-reference selection occurs on development or uses simultaneous comparisons.

V4-55.12.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-55.12.text: Optional analyses MUST be labeled exploratory and cannot retroactively redefine a failed primary gate.

V4-56.01.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.01.text: S0 MAY qualify with 1,000 measured queries; S1–S4 MUST use at least 10,000. Independent restart repetitions and declared warmup excluded from reported samples are required in every envelope.

V4-56.02.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.02.text: Query mixes MUST include exact, semantic paraphrase, temporal, multi-entity, no-answer, procedural, and cross-scope authorized cases.

V4-56.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-56.03.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.03.text: Performance qualification MUST preserve retrieval quality within one percentage point of the completed exact/reference run on the paired evaluation set.

V4-56.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-56.04.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.04.text: The 4,096/4,097-span boundary MUST be tested explicitly; internal batching limits cannot disable an otherwise valid lane.

V4-56.05.note: test module docstring claims coverage in tests/eval/test_v4_envelopes.py; no named check (V4-61.02)
V4-56.05.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.05.text: Capture acknowledgment p95 MUST target at most 50 ms for accepted 4 KiB textual inputs without synchronous model inference.

V4-56.06.note: test module docstring claims coverage in tests/eval/test_v4_envelopes.py; no named check (V4-61.02)
V4-56.06.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.06.text: At S1/S2 sustained load, lexical readiness p95 MUST target two seconds and local semantic readiness ten seconds, with failures and backlog fully reported.

V4-56.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-56.07.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.07.text: Suppression acknowledgment p95 MUST target 100 ms under the declared mixed load; physical closure is separately measured and remains resumable.

V4-56.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-56.08.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.08.text: Local inference concurrency MUST honor a configured RAM ceiling; peak RSS, artifact RAM, and storage amplification MUST be published.

V4-56.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-56.09.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.09.text: Default foreground requests MUST remain bounded during reindex, consolidation, rotation, and purge; no target may be met by suppressing required receipts.

V4-56.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-56.10.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.10.text: CPU, energy where measurable, token, currency, disk, and operator-work costs MUST accompany throughput claims.

V4-56.11.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.11.text: A failed capacity envelope MUST narrow supported deployment claims or trigger architectural work, not a silent SLO increase.

V4-56.12.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-56.12.section_title: Workload envelopes, performance, and resource targets
V4-56.12.text: One-million-token and one-million-claim workloads MUST not be treated as equivalent; both source volume and materialized expansion are measured.

V4-57.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-57.01.text: Deterministic suites MUST test every verb/purpose/scope combination across all shipped read, write, export, learning, cache, and transport paths.

V4-57.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-57.02.text: Metamorphic tests MUST preserve authorized outputs when unrelated unauthorized corpora change, including lexical statistics and learned-policy state.

V4-57.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-57.03.text: Race tests MUST interleave revoke, quarantine, purge, correction, lease loss, and delivery/dispatch at every relevant checkpoint.

V4-57.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-57.04.text: Poisoning suites MUST include direct writes, documents, tool output, agent notes, summaries, compiled procedures, and cross-session delayed retrieval.

V4-57.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-57.05.text: Assembled-context tests MUST include benign items whose combination changes meaning, as well as legitimate runbooks and safety instructions.

V4-57.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-57.06.text: Sensitive-data evaluation MUST separate detection misses from routing/authorization violations for detected or declared values.

V4-57.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-57.07.text: Deletion probes MUST test exact recall, semantic recall, reconstruction from derivatives, caches, replay, exports, indexes, and restored snapshots.

V4-57.08.text: Defensive benchmarks MUST report attack success, action-use success on a sandbox host, and retained benign utility with cluster-aware uncertainty.

V4-57.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-57.09.text: Each advertised language and deployment profile MUST pass its own relevant safety slice; English stdio tests cannot certify multilingual HTTP behavior.

V4-57.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-57.10.text: Independent security review MUST inspect the enforcement kernel and real integration paths, not only the threat-model document.

V4-58.01.note: test module docstring claims coverage in tests/v4/test_scenarios_d.py; no named check (V4-61.02)
V4-58.01.text: Every applicable scenario MUST execute through the actual public integration it claims to cover and retain a requirement-tagged result.

V4-58.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-58.02.text: Scenarios with races MUST use deterministic scheduling hooks plus stress runs; a timing-sensitive test that rarely reaches the race is insufficient.

V4-58.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-58.03.text: Skipped, xfailed, unavailable, and deselected cases MUST remain visible and cannot count toward a passing scenario denominator.

V4-58.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-58.04.text: Requirements not anchored in this table MUST still have direct checks under the exhaustive §61 ledger; the table is not a substitute for complete traceability.

V4-58.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-58.05.text: M0 MUST execute C01–C32, C35, C52, C54–C64, C71, C73, C76, C77, and C81–C93 on the registered path; remaining C rows bind the milestone that first exposes their capability.

V4-58.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-58.06.text: After each milestone, the release report MUST name the strongest held-out losses and the smallest next change that addresses them.

V4-59.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-59.01.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.01.text: M0 / v4.0 MUST pass G4-00, G4-01, G4-06 on S0, G4-07, G4-11, and G4-13 for reachable capabilities. G4-02 and G4-03 bind M1; G4-04 binds M2; G4-05 binds M3; G4-08 and G4-09 bind M4; G4-10 and G4-14 bind M5. Disabled later features do not waive their later milestone.

V4-59.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-59.02.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.02.text: A quality-leadership claim MUST show at least a three-percentage-point primary utility gain over each named comparator, with simultaneous lower confidence bounds above zero.

V4-59.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-59.03.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.03.text: Near-ceiling workloads MAY use a preregistered frontier claim: quality non-inferior within one point and at least 20% lower total cost or p95 latency.

V4-59.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-59.04.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.04.text: Leadership MUST also preserve safety gates and avoid more than two points of quality regression on any preregistered critical category or language.

V4-59.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-59.05.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.05.text: Frontier improvements MUST not conceal an unbounded regression elsewhere; all quality, cost, latency, privacy, and operator-burden axes remain published.

V4-59.06.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.06.text: A provider without a valid executed comparison MUST be listed as untested/unavailable; it cannot be included among defeated competitors.

V4-59.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-59.07.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.07.text: Claims expire after 90 days or material comparator/model changes unless reconfirmed; the competitor registry must be refreshed first.

V4-59.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-59.08.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.08.text: Broad market-leadership language MUST require G4-14 and a published tested-market definition, never claim victory over unknown future providers.

V4-59.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-59.09.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.09.text: If a leadership gate fails, the release MAY ship only with narrower factual capability claims and the negative results visible.

V4-59.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-59.10.section_title: Release gates and competitive leadership gates
V4-59.10.text: No privacy or integrity failure may be traded for a better aggregate benchmark score.

V4-60.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-60.01.section_title: Implementation waves, ownership, and stop/go criteria
V4-60.01.text: W1 MUST precede production qualification of any new learning or retrieval feature that depends on the repaired boundaries.

V4-60.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-60.02.section_title: Implementation waves, ownership, and stop/go criteria
V4-60.02.text: Parallel implementation MAY occur only behind frozen contracts and disjoint ownership; integration proof remains mandatory for each slice.

V4-60.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-60.03.section_title: Implementation waves, ownership, and stop/go criteria
V4-60.03.text: A wave MUST not exit on imported modules, schema presence, or unit counts alone; observable product behavior and failure recovery are required.

V4-60.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-60.04.section_title: Implementation waves, ownership, and stop/go criteria
V4-60.04.text: Dependencies MUST have typed unavailable behavior from the start; missing mandatory controls cannot be treated as optional modules.

V4-60.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-60.05.section_title: Implementation waves, ownership, and stop/go criteria
V4-60.05.text: Failed gates MUST produce an explicit blocker, diagnosis, and retest plan; unrelated feature expansion cannot obscure the blocker.

V4-60.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-60.06.section_title: Implementation waves, ownership, and stop/go criteria
V4-60.06.text: User-facing configuration or compatibility changes MUST include migration impact and an opt-in rollout plan before release.

V4-60.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-60.07.section_title: Implementation waves, ownership, and stop/go criteria
V4-60.07.text: Research spending and remote execution MUST require a separately approved budget and corpus/license plan.

V4-60.08.section_title: Implementation waves, ownership, and stop/go criteria
V4-60.08.text: Each wave MUST include simplification review: remove duplicate paths and retire mechanisms whose benefit failed measurement.

V4-60.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-60.09.section_title: Implementation waves, ownership, and stop/go criteria
V4-60.09.text: W0 MUST include package discovery and `register()` tests; W2 MUST qualify the registered Hermes path. Shipping W0–W2 internals while leaving `register()` on the older engine fails the wave.

V4-61.01.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.01.text: Each requirement MUST have an exhaustive manifest row linking capability, tier, owner, code path, tests, datasets, scenarios, gates, and current status.

V4-61.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.02.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.02.text: Test files or section markers alone MUST not satisfy a requirement; named assertions must exercise its observable behavior.

V4-61.03.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.03.text: The ledger generator MUST reject unknown IDs, duplicate IDs, missing applicable mappings, stale artifact hashes, and false verified statuses.

V4-61.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.04.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.04.text: Boundary tests MUST be parameterized over object kind, surface, lifecycle, scope, purpose, hold state, and recovery phase where applicable.

V4-61.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.05.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.05.text: Mutation tests MUST remove quote checks, purpose filters, digest checks, lease fences, erasure checks, and budget checks and observe test failures.

V4-61.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.06.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.06.text: Property tests MUST generate delegation, graph, temporal, duplicate-delivery, and cancellation histories against a small reference state machine.

V4-61.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.07.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.07.text: Differential tests MUST compare direct API, SDK, MCP, export, and service outcomes using the same authenticated operation stream.

V4-61.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.08.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.08.text: CI MUST forbid direct evidence SQL outside approved boundaries, duplicated policy helpers, network on import, and undeclared transport clients.

V4-61.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.09.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.09.text: Full qualification MUST run from a clean environment without inherited credentials or live host state, plus a separate actual socket-denial test.

V4-61.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.10.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.10.text: Performance smoke tests MAY use wider regression thresholds, but release gates MUST consume independently measured actual SLO results.

V4-61.11.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.11.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.11.text: Quarantined/flaky tests MUST remain visible blockers for affected critical requirements; repeated reruns until green are not qualification.

V4-61.12.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-61.12.section_title: Executable traceability, mutation tests, and CI
V4-61.12.text: New object types MUST fail CI until access, provenance, invalidation, erasure, serialization, migration, and recovery tests are registered.

V4-62.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-62.01.text: Canonical evidence fidelity, explicit consent, scoped authority, durable receipts, and honest erasure remain non-negotiable predecessor invariants.

V4-62.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-62.02.text: V4 explicitly permits optional generated derived views under §20, replacing the older blanket producer restriction only for separately enabled derivatives.

V4-62.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-62.03.text: Existing sources, spans, claims, revisions, and source identifiers MUST be preserved unless the operator approves a documented erasure or repair.

V4-62.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-62.04.text: Read-only grants MUST not be silently widened to quote; migration MUST report callers whose former unsafe behavior will now deny.

V4-62.05.text: Ambiguous empty-purpose grants and unauthenticated checker outcomes MUST be quarantined or mapped conservatively, with owner-reviewed remediation.

V4-62.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-62.06.text: Existing derivative ancestry MUST be audited; missing edges cannot be fabricated from plausible text and must produce unverified/withheld objects.

V4-62.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-62.07.text: Existing plaintext sensitive values MUST receive an explicit reviewed migration plan; enabling a vault cannot claim prior copies vanished.

V4-62.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-62.08.text: Config migration MUST leave capture, remote processors, synthesis, sharing, and automatic promotion disabled unless prior explicit equivalent authorization is proven.

V4-62.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-62.09.text: Migration MUST provide dry-run impact, backup/key checks, lock requirements, resumable phases, verification, and rollback-before-cutover instructions.

V4-62.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-62.10.text: V1/V2/V3 regression suites remain relevant except documented intentional security/contract changes; unsafe behavior is not a compatibility obligation.

V4-63.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.01.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.01.text: Core packaging MUST preserve Python 3.11+ compatibility unless a separately reviewed compatibility change states the new minimum.

V4-63.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.02.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.02.text: Optional extras MUST isolate local neural inference, local synthesis, service transport, PostgreSQL, workbench, and host-specific dependencies.

V4-63.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.03.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.03.text: The initial local neural runtime SHOULD be reviewed ONNX Runtime CPU; artifact/model selection requires the §29 bake-off and license review, not brand preference.

V4-63.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.04.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.04.text: Dependencies and model artifacts MUST be pinned in release manifests, scanned, and accompanied by an SBOM and provenance records.

V4-63.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.05.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.05.text: New dependencies SHOULD have at least seven days of public release history; existing repository security controls cannot be weakened to install them.

V4-63.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.06.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.06.text: Runtime artifact loading MUST prohibit remote code execution, automatic downloads, unreviewed pickle loading, and unbounded archive extraction.

V4-63.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.07.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.07.text: Releases MUST include compatible schemas, CLI help, migration tools, fixture generators, evaluation runners, and license notices.

V4-63.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.08.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.08.text: Proprietary hosted comparators and restricted datasets MUST remain external integrations, not redistributed inside the OSS package without permission.

V4-63.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.09.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.09.text: Supported OS/CPU/runtime matrices MUST be measured; a local-first claim cannot assume one developer's virtual environment.

V4-63.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-63.10.section_title: Packaging, supply chain, and open-source delivery
V4-63.10.text: Example configuration and tests MUST contain no real credentials, private histories, live endpoints requiring payment, or automatic provider activation.

V4-64.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.01.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.01.text: Rollout MUST begin with disposable-store conformance, then owner-approved shadow comparison, then bounded opt-in activation.

V4-64.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.02.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.02.text: Shadow runs MUST not disclose additional private data or spend remote budget without explicit authorization.

V4-64.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.03.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.03.text: Feature kill switches MUST disable optional producers/routes without disabling integrity, suppression, or revocation controls.

V4-64.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.04.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.04.text: Incident response MUST support scope lockdown, permit revocation, quarantine expansion, producer suspension, and influence-based impact enumeration.

V4-64.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.05.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.05.text: A corruption incident MUST preserve diagnostic evidence safely and stop unverified serving; an operator override cannot silently label corrupt content verified.

V4-64.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.06.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.06.text: Privacy incidents MUST identify recipients, purposes, affected revisions, external copies, and restoration/erasure limits without duplicating sensitive payloads.

V4-64.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.07.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.07.text: Capacity incidents MUST distinguish writer contention, inference saturation, checkpoint starvation, and queue imbalance before backend migration is recommended.

V4-64.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.08.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.08.text: Release rollback MUST preserve new deletion knowledge and never reopen a store with software that cannot enforce its current security state.

V4-64.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.09.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.09.text: Runbooks MUST cover locked keys, denied egress, missing models, failed migrations, growing closure backlog, unavailable comparators, and failed quality gates.

V4-64.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-64.10.section_title: Rollout, incident response, and operating runbooks
V4-64.10.text: Every production-facing default change MUST have a measurable rollout criterion and rollback trigger tied to utility, privacy, and resource outcomes.

V4-65.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.01.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.01.text: HRR, learned controllers, sparse/late retrieval, and automatic procedure promotion MUST retain independent ablation and safety gates.

V4-65.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.02.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.02.text: Multi-writer replication, federated learning, and parameter-updated memory MUST remain research until revocation and deletion semantics are specified and tested.

V4-65.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.03.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.03.text: Fine-tuning on private memory MUST default prohibited; owners must separately authorize training, retention, export, and unlearning limitations.

V4-65.04.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.04.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.04.text: No latent representation or compressed bank may become the only surviving evidence for a factual claim.

V4-65.05.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.05.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.05.text: A feature without measurable advantage MUST not stay on by default merely because a competitor advertises it.

V4-65.06.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.06.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.06.text: Manual approval of every low-risk fact MUST not be presented as successful automation; review burden participates in utility and release gates.

V4-65.07.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.07.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.07.text: Refusing all suspicious or unknown content MUST not count as competitive safety when benign utility collapses.

V4-65.08.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.08.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.08.text: Additional schema, abstractions, and profiles MUST receive a complexity budget and a named deletion/recovery owner before acceptance.

V4-65.09.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.09.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.09.text: No hidden LLM loop, silent backend fallback, fabricated checker attestation, or global trust score may be introduced as a shortcut to benchmark success.

V4-65.10.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-65.10.section_title: Research boundaries, simplification, and rejected shortcuts
V4-65.10.text: The program MUST prefer removing duplicated mechanisms over adding another enforcement layer around them.

V4-66.01.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-66.01.text: Every externally motivated design claim MUST identify whether it comes from documentation, inspected code, a paper, or executed evidence.

V4-66.02.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-66.02.text: Links and abstracts MUST not be treated as complete implementation audits, license reviews, or independent benchmark reproduction.

V4-66.03.note: no implementation or test evidence registered
V4-66.03.text: Comparator and model manifests MUST pin actual immutable revisions during implementation; mutable main branches are discovery references only.
